This cursed place serves as a sort of crucible for an ooze-worshiping cult. Those who survive are granted a boon from the Slime Lord. Those who do not, wander the halls as the unquiet dead, doomed to serve the ooze for eternity.

Design, writing, map and layout by Jordan Rudd.

https://jordanrudd.itch.io/

Art by Jeri Honeywell

Boon of the Slime Lord.description: When anyone with this boon encounters an ooze or slime-related creature, they may make a reaction roll and add 4 to the result in addition to any other bonuses. On a modified result of 12 or greater, the creature is charmed for [[/r 1d4]] rounds.
Boon of the Slime Lord.name: Boon of the Slime Lord

Marasoda, The Sludge Slayer.description:
This indestructible magic warhammer has a broad head carved with intricate geometric patterns and an ironwood haft. It does triple damage against oozes and slimes.

It was wielded by the ooze-fighting hero Domhnall O’Dunn. He was eventually murdered by the cult, who then stole the hammer and hid it away.
Marasoda, The Sludge Slayer.name: Marasoda, The Sludge Slayer

Scroll of Burning Hands.description:
You spread your fingers with thumbs touching, unleashing a circle of flame that fills a close area around where you stand.

Creatures within the area of effect take 1d6 damage.

Unattended flammable objects ignite.
Scroll of Burning Hands.name: Scroll of Burning Hands

Slime-Proof Holy Symbol of Madeera.description: This holy symbol is made of brightly polished brass that will never tarnish. It has been specially blessed to repel oozes and slimes in near range. Any lawful character may make a DC 11 WIS spellcasting check to rebuke such creatures, forcing them to flee. Targets must make a CHA check opposed by the spellcasting check or flee from for 5 rounds. On a failed spellcasting check, the symbol cannot be used again until the next day.
Slime-Proof Holy Symbol of Madeera.name: Slime-Proof Holy Symbol of Madeera

The Trusty Helm.description:
A dented but sound steel spangenhelm with two great, black-tipped aurochs horns. 

Whenever anyone wearing this helmet is hit with a critical hit, the damage will never take them below 1 hp.
The Trusty Helm.name: The Trusty Helm

Torch.description: Sheds light to a near distance (see Light Sources, pg. 46). Burns for one hour of real time.
Torch.name: Torch

Jellied Skeleton.description:
A bleach-boned skeleton covered in a thin, green-tinted jelly.

AC 13 (chainmail), HP 11, ATK acidic touch +1 (1d4) or 1 bastard sword +1 (1d10), MV near, S +1, D +0, C +2, I -2, W +0, Ch -1, AL C, LV 2

Undead. Immune to morale checks.
Jellied Skeleton.name: Jellied Skeleton

Jellied Undead.description: Immune to morale checks, poison and acid.
Jellied Undead.name: Jellied Undead

A translucent cube of slime that silently mows through cramped tunnels, slurping up debris.

AC 11, HP 24, ATK 1 touch +4 (1d8 + toxin), MV near S +3, D +1, C +2, I -4, W +1, Ch -4, AL N, LV 5

Engulf. Absorbs paralyzed creatures in close range into its body, automatically hitting with touch attack on its turn.

Rubbery. Half damage from stabbing weapons.

Toxin. DC 15 CON or paralyzed 1d4 rounds.
Raka Ooku.name: Raka Ooku

Engulf.description: DC 12 STR or become trapped inside the cube. Touch attack auto-hits engulfed targets each round. DC 12 STR on turn to escape.
Engulf.name: Engulf

Rubbery.description: Half damage from stabbing weapons.
Rubbery.name: Rubbery

Skeletons.description: 1d3 Jellied Skeletons inside. Each round, 1:3 chance one escapes and enters combat.

Necrotic.name: Necrotic

Long, multi-limbed monster arthropods that have adapted to the prey found in this dungeon.

AC 12, HP 18, ATK 1 bite +2 (1d8), MV near (climb), S +2, D +2, C +0, I -3, W +1, Ch -3, AL N, LV 4

Ooze-proof: Immune to poison and acid.
Slime Eater.name: Slime Eater

Hard-bitten rogue in tattered leathers and a hooded cloak.

Background.name: Background
Background.text: This cursed place serves as a sort of crucible for an ooze-worshiping cult. Those who survive are granted a boon from the Slime Lord. Those who do not, wander the halls as the unquiet dead, doomed to serve the ooze for eternity. The player characters have just been kidnapped from their village and thrown in a pit to face the Trial of the Slime Lord. The adventure begins as the cultists slide a heavy stone lid over an opening in the ceiling of @UUID[.1moVU3Fic8mrMfok]{Area 1}. With nothing more than their wits and the clothes on their backs, they must escape or die.

Area 1: The Pit.name: Area 1: The Pit
Area 1: The Pit.text:
A single torch lying on the floor sheds light on the glistening, slime-slick stone walls of this round chamber and on the terrified faces of a dozen of your fellow villagers. The sound of running water echoes faintly through a foreboding dark archway to the south . Words carved into the archway read: “WELCOME TO DISSOLUTION. ESCAPE OR FEED RAKA OOKU.” @UUID[Macro.l3RzjQ1yv10GXGYA]{Display Area 1 Carving}

  • Torch: A mundane torch has been tossed down by the ooze cultists. Start the torch timer when a PC picks it up.

  • Floor: One large tile along the western wall makes a faint hollow sound. DC 18 WIS to find if the floor is checked. PCs will need something heavy and strong to smash it (like a hammer) or a crowbar to pry it up. Smashing the tile makes noise - roll [[/r 1d3]] on the @UUID[.qryjGsZPGxBXIy94]{Random Encounters} table. The passageway beneath it leads to @UUID[.OlHSrCg85LxqRsCS]{Area 17}.

  • Walls: Searching the walls turns up a torn journal page, rolled up and hidden in a crack. It reads “...told us that not all the slime is bad, and some can be eaten for…”@UUID[Macro.crWvKgh9FOBjC2L5]

Running the Adventure.name: Running the Adventure
Running the Adventure.text:
• I recommend that each player “owns” 2-3 characters, but that in each round they choose only one character to act, including combat rounds. This helps to keep things moving and manage the action economy.

  • The primary goal of the players is to escape through the doors in @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15}. The two parts of the incantation needed to open the doors are in @UUID[.oCe5g1GoEsnAjmgh]{Area 8} and @UUID[.dhMrZiocfh0OoweI]{Area 11}.

  • This adventure uses the term “PC-rounds”. A PC-round is the amount of work a PC can do in one round. If a task requires 3 PC-rounds, it could be 1 PC working for 3 rounds or 3 PCs working for 1 round, or any combination thereof.

  • Unless otherwise stated, all areas are dark and all doors are unlocked.

  • All ooze/slime/mucous/gelatin encountered in this adventure is harmful against organic material only, unless stated otherwise. It does not harm metal or stone.

  • @UUID[Actor.N4D3VFipYl5a4Dbo]{Raka Ooku} is a necrotic cube. It retreats after engulfing a single PC and will afterwards ignore the rest of PCs unless they attack. Once the characters open the door in @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15} it will no longer retreat.

  • @UUID[Actor.NbZafG36BrxiP9wA]{The Collector} is a demented halfling that underwent the trial many years ago. He succeeded but was driven mad. Now he walks the halls of the dungeon collecting anything he can find. Years spent underground have adapted him to the darkness. The slimes don’t attack him but he avoids the @UUID[Actor.T1001So6LnoVL7sO]{Slime Eaters}, @UUID[.rjha846tW6Hs2OTu]{Area 7} and the @UUID[Item.S2hNs23QCZOaVwCZ]{holy symbol of Madeera} found in @UUID[.hDQxEQg2dN17uW9a]{Area 14}. He will snatch up anything left unattended by the players and take it to @UUID[.9Wjdq52LDykYoDH5]{Area 2}.

  • All monsters stop pursuing players when they are out of sight.

@UUID[.qryjGsZPGxBXIy94]{Random Encounters}

Area 2: The Collection.name: Area 2: The Collection
Area 2: The Collection.text:
The door is slightly ajar. Piles of garbage and detritus are haphazardly heaped against the walls and corners of the otherwise plain room. There appears to be a few useful items mixed in with the trash. Several sticky, humanoid-sized footprints mark the floor.

  • The first time the PCs visit this room, @UUID[Actor.NbZafG36BrxiP9wA]{The Collector} will not be present. On every subsequent visit there is a 3 in 6 chance he will be here, and a 1 in 6 chance he will be asleep. He does not take kindly to thieves.

  • The Collector is a wiry, pale-skinned halfling dressed in rags. His large eyes are milky-white and his skin is constantly wet with a foul-smelling mucus. He carries a cruelly serrated dagger and wears a polished piece of hardened gray ooze around his neck. It is one of the keys used in @UUID[.HMTikwW0DRE8EngW]{Area 12} to unlock @UUID[.DSAvjULwx5at49km]{Area 16}. If attacked he uses his Stealthy trait to escape, but will defend @UUID[.9Wjdq52LDykYoDH5]{Area 2} to the death

  • Piles: The first time a PC searches, allow them to roll twice on the @UUID[RollTable.88YONanX0anxFcy3]{Random Gear} Table. For every round they search thereafter, there is a 2 in 6 chance of finding something useful. Roll on the Random Gear Table if successful.

  • Footprints: Are of a barefoot human or something with human-sized feet. They appear to be recent.

    The Collector

Area 3: The Statues.name: Area 3: The Statues
Area 3: The Statues.text:
Three lumpy and misshapen statues near the east wall cast ominous shadows. Each one depicts a humanoid figure undergoing some kind of slime-related trauma. The sound of running water echoes from the northeast passage.

  • Statues: Made of some kind of chalky, pale green substance. They hint at the ritual to be performed in @UUID[.oCe5g1GoEsnAjmgh]{Area 8}. In order of north to south, the statues are:

    • A man half-covered in slime that dissolves the flesh from his bones. His arms are raised in exultation and there is joyous expression on what remains of his face. A plaque on the plinth reads “The first offering is flesh”.

    • The upper half of a skeleton rises from an unidentifiable puddle. Its arms are also raised and its jaw hangs open. A plaque on the plinth reads “The second offering is bone”.

    • A waste-high pile of ooze with three depressions suggesting a face with empty eyes and a gaping mouth. A plaque on the plinth reads “The final offering is all”.

    Searching around the statues also uncovers the torn page of a journal. It reads: “…sn’t come to that. The first two offerings are bad enough. But I don’t think we could live with ourselves if we made the third offering. Besides, what living things could we find down there?”@UUID[Macro.njXDupDJ8J5aGySI]

The Statues

Area 4: The Drain.name: Area 4: The Drain
Area 4: The Drain.text:
Clear, cool, knee-deep water circles around a rusty grate in the floor. Roots dangle from cracks in the sagging stone ceiling.

  • Grate: Covers the drain where water flows outside. A few small bones rest on it. Anyone examining the grate will see a tarnished brass key just on the other side, wedged in a rock. The key unlocks the door to @UUID[.avoIM80L2A7PBs8V]{Area 13}. Removing the grate requires a crowbar or 6 PC-rounds.

If the characters attempt to escape via the drain, the passageway is small enough that only a halfling or goblin will fit. They must make a DC 18 CON or drown. If they succeed, they emerge in a stream far away from the dungeon and from danger.

Area 5: The Pool.name: Area 5: The Pool
Area 5: The Pool.text:
The water in this chamber moves over large bones littering the stone floor in a slow but steady current towards @UUID[.E10dIyCTD8CnW8IL]{Area 4}. The ceiling is low and cramped.

  • A @UUID[Actor.RPM59pNQewkLSI6s]{translucent ooze} lurks in the water. It will attack after one round or when someone tries to leave, seeking the weakest character. It will not leave the water.

  • Water: Knee-deep. Anyone observing the water for a few moments will notice small spots where it seems to move against the flow as the ooze swims around.

  • Bones: Appear to be humanoid, completely clean.

Area 6: The Waterfall.name: Area 6: The Waterfall
Area 6: The Waterfall.text:
Water cascades out of a sludge-caked pipe in the ceiling and onto the ground.

  • Water: Any uncovered torches will be doused when passing through this area and cannot be relit.

  • Pipe: Too slick and too steep to climb.

Area 7: The Dripping Caves.name: Area 7: The Dripping Caves
Area 7: The Dripping Caves.text:
Irregular drips fall from dagger-like stalactites and land with a soft hiss. A corpse lies along the southern wall next to a fat backpack.

  • Drips: Highly corrosive. DC 12 DEX or take 1d4 damage each round or when moving through the room.

  • Corpse: Male dwarf, has been here for several months. Hole bored into the top of his skull. He has a staff in one hand and a polished piece of hardened black ooze in the other. It is one of the keys used in @UUID[.HMTikwW0DRE8EngW]{Area 12} to unlock @UUID[.DSAvjULwx5at49km]{Area 16}.

  • Backpack: In addition to a @UUID[Item.zkQrGwmOIu8fRKg4]{Scroll of Burning Hands}, and a torch, roll [[/r 2d6]] twice on the @UUID[RollTable.88YONanX0anxFcy3]{Random Gear} Table to determine contents.

Area 8: The Offering Chamber.name: Area 8: The Offering Chamber
Area 8: The Offering Chamber.text:
The center of this room is dominated by a raised pool of viscous green fluid that stews and boils. The scent burns your nostrils and makes your eyes water. Three crude bas-reliefs cover the south wall depicting a man being consumed by ooze.

  • Bas reliefs: Scenes resemble the statues in @UUID[.WRe2soOEKkUQTlqd]{Area 3}.

  • Pool: Filled with highly corrosive slime. Three offerings must be made in order to reveal the first part of the incantation needed to open the doors in @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15}:

    1. Flesh - any living flesh, must cause at least 1 damage.

    2. Bone - any bone. 

    3. All - an entire living thing. Possibilities include a villager, a rat, a slime eater or even a PC. Bugs don’t count.

Each offering lowers the level of slime in the pool. When the offerings are complete, the pool drains and the words are revealed on the bottom: “O Slime Lord, open the way before us; Dissolve us in thine glutinous glory”. @UUID[Macro.11ofJcTNj0B22YIx] The door to @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15} also opens. The pool refills after 1 round.

Area 9: The Fetid Pool.name: Area 9: The Fetid Pool
Area 9: The Fetid Pool.text:
A dank natural cavern with a low ceiling. The stench of rot wafts off of a pool of fetid water collecting in a shallow depression. The passage to the north is filled with dirt and stone piled nearly to the ceiling.

  • Pool: Examining the pool will reveal that it is filled with mud and detritus. Searching for 1 round has a 2 in 6 chance of finding a piece of @UUID[RollTable.88YONanX0anxFcy3]{Random Gear}.

  • Passage: Caved-in. Takes 15 PC-rounds to clear by hand or 10 with a shovel. 1 in 6 chance of another cave-in for each round - DC 12 DEX or 1d4 damage and restarts the effort to clear the passage. This cave-in will only happen once.

  • Dirt: Scrap of paper is half-buried but visible. It reads “...f we can’t go back the way we came, someone will have to eat the orange sli…”. @UUID[Macro.hQRvYCgCyD6f1Dwb]{Display Scrap Paper (Area 9)}

Area 10: The Slime Eaters.name: Area 10: The Slime Eaters
Area 10: The Slime Eaters.text:
Two human-sized centipedes along the northwest wall suck the slime from a collection of bleached bones. Behind them, a vaguely humanoid form is slumped on the floor.

  • Centipedes: These creatures are @UUID[Actor.T1001So6LnoVL7sO]{Slime Eaters} - long, multi-limbed monster arthropods that have adapted to the prey found in this dungeon. They ignore non-ooze creatures unless they come into close range. They can also smell any ooze or slime in near range and will follow it. The Slime Eaters retreat through cracks in the cave walls at ½ hp and return when the coast is clear.

  • Form: The skeleton of an unfortunate human female adventurer. Her pack is mostly dissolved but contains an intact straight peen hammer, a torch and burned scrap of paper that reads “..egendary weapon ...ced on the altar. We have the keys…” @UUID[Macro.V2IONSSG3bPqgBYd]{Display Scrap Paper (Area 10)}. She wears a polished piece of hardened yellow ooze on a cord around her neck. It is one of the keys used in @UUID[.HMTikwW0DRE8EngW]{Area 12} to unlock @UUID[.DSAvjULwx5at49km]{Area 16}.

Slime Eaters

Area 11: The Consumption Chamber.name: Area 11: The Consumption Chamber
Area 11: The Consumption Chamber.text:
Murals carved into the wall depict scenes of ooze cultists gorging themselves on slime that runs out of their overfilled mouths and onto the floor. A clumpy, pale green statue of a robed figure stands with its back to the west wall. A stone bowl lies at its feet.

  • Murals: Contain a series of strange, indecipherable runes.

  • Statue: Holds an amphora from which a trickle of orange slime continuously flows into the bowl.

  • Bowl: Filled with orange slime. The slime is mostly harmless, but consuming it causes severe hallucinations for [[/r 1d4]] rounds. The walls seem to melt and flow and other peoples’ flesh turns into translucent jelly. The murals also come alive, and the formerly indecipherable runes form the first part of the incantation needed to open the doors in @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15}: “Consume us that we may consume; And fill us with thine viscous victuals”. @UUID[Macro.PI89wEmj2VYs1UYm]{Display Strange Runes (Area 11)}

Anyone consuming the slime must also make a DC 15 WIS. On failure they cannot maintain and must roll on the @UUID[RollTable.zVcS5cR0lCv9XqM4]{slime effects} table.

d4

Things That Happen When You’re Tripping Balls on Psychedelic Slime

1

You go berserk and attack the nearest person for 2 rounds.

2

You run screaming out of the room, roll a @UUID[JournalEntry.FprNeOJ2mcSRv7Pl.JournalEntryPage.qryjGsZPGxBXIy94]{Random Encounters}

3

You’ll never be right in the head again. Permanent -1 to WIS.

4

The boundary between you and the universe disappears. Permanent +1 to WIS.

Area 12: The Alter.name: Area 12: The Alter
Area 12: The Alter.text:
Four skeletons covered in a thin, green-tinted jelly stand at attention. They flank a rough-hewn, tri-color altar made of a shiny, semi-translucent substance. The walls are decorated with murals depicting a great battle and there is a metal door in the south wall.

  • Skeletons: Attack anyone entering the room. One wields a bastard sword engraved with an onyx in the crossguard worth 25 gp.

  • Altar: Made of three, similarly-sized, dried slime cubes - yellow, black and gray. Always hot to the touch. When one of the chunks of hardened ooze found in @UUID[.rjha846tW6Hs2OTu]{Area 7}, @UUID[.6qBkvcHVNZVw9k0m]{Area 10} or on @UUID[Actor.NbZafG36BrxiP9wA]{The Collector} is placed on the corresponding part of the altar, it will melt into the block. When all three have been melted, the door to @UUID[.DSAvjULwx5at49km]{Area 16} will open.

  • Murals: Various slime creatures prevailing against a human army led by a sinister-looking warrior wielding a large warhammer.

  • Door: Locked. The key is in @UUID[.E10dIyCTD8CnW8IL]{Area 4}. Forcing the door requires a DC 18 STR (crowbar grants advantage). For each attempt roll a d3 on the @UUID[.qryjGsZPGxBXIy94]{Random Encounter} table.

Area 13: The Armory.name: Area 13: The Armory
Area 13: The Armory.text:
A couple of mostly-empty weapon racks and armor stands in an otherwise plain room. What items remain are dented, corroded and blunted.

  • Weapon Racks: 2 usable @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.brIFMH0sOVmqX02N]{spears} and 1 usable @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.KQTWQwznjK80gVEU]{shortsword}. Everything else is damaged beyond use.

  • Armor Stands: A badly damaged shirt of chainmail that functions as @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.EoTEHXApVDS7rHfw]{leather armor}, and @UUID[Item.8bxAQncf9MtbhC4S]{The Trusty Helm} that grants advantage to avoid damage from the corrosive drips in @UUID[.rjha846tW6Hs2OTu]{Area 7}.

Area 14: The Drop.name: Area 14: The Drop
Area 14: The Drop.text:
Coming from @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15}, there is a 40’ drop into a small round room. The walls sweat a thick, sticky mucus that runs down onto the floor. A body lies in a broken heap next to a frayed rope.

  • Mucus: Inert but gross. Anyone covered in the mucus will not be attacked by @UUID[Actor.ulNxYSQR6AqenuIC]{Jellied Skeletons} but will definitely be attacked by @UUID[Actor.T1001So6LnoVL7sO]{Slime Eater}. This effect lasts 4 rounds. Covering takes 1 round and the player must make a DC 12 CON or spend an additional round vomiting prodigiously.

  • Body: Human female adventurer. There is a @UUID[Item.S2hNs23QCZOaVwCZ]{Slime-Proof Holy Symbol of Madeera} around her neck and a knobbed @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.jGZyVuFJnW7QcBFX]{mace} attached to her belt. She wears a backpack - in addition to a @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.magic-items.Item.jucTGEjsqJ1znHdf]{potion of healing}, roll 2d6 twice on the @UUID[RollTable.88YONanX0anxFcy3]{Random Gear} Table to determine contents.

Area 15: The Door.name: Area 15: The Door
Area 15: The Door.text:
Massive double doors of tarnished bronze are flanked by sconces burning with low, flickering embers. Across the top is written “SPEAK DEVOTION TO THE SLIME LORD AND PASS”. Some worn letters or symbols have been scratched into the stone floor

  • Sconces: Very firmly attached to the wall. Will continue to burn as long as they remain in place, otherwise they burn out in 30 minutes.

  • Letters: Someone once scratched the entire incantation in the middle of the floor, but it was hastily removed. Only the first 2 or 3 letters of each line remain.

  • Secret Door: There is a secret door to @UUID[.oCe5g1GoEsnAjmgh]{Area 8}. Searching the walls next to the X’s on the map will reveal two stones that can be depressed. The door opens if they are pressed simultaneously, and slams closed immediately when one is released.

  • Doors: Decorated with reliefs that depict horrific scenes of cultists devouring and being dissolved by ooze. They will open when both parts of the incantation are spoken aloud in the room (found in @UUID[.oCe5g1GoEsnAjmgh]{Area 8} and @UUID[.dhMrZiocfh0OoweI]{Area 11}):

    • “O Slime Lord, open the way before us
      Dissolve us in thine glutinous glory
      Consume us that we may consume
      And fill us with thine viscous victuals”

The door opens as soon as the incantation is spoken, @UUID[Actor.N4D3VFipYl5a4Dbo]{Raka Ooku} will appear in the hallway to the north, just outside the room. Roll initiative immediately - the door takes 3 combat rounds to open wide enough for the PCs to escape. Raka Ooku will not leave the dungeon but will remain in the room after the door has been opened. If the PCs escape, go to @UUID[.sifWzGHWaOKPay91]{The Aftermath}.

Raka Ooku

Area 16: The Hammer.name: Area 16: The Hammer
Area 16: The Hammer.text:
A warhammer is suspended in a cube of translucent, green-tinted gelatin that rests on a stone table in the middle of the room. Strange runes cover the walls.

  • Warhammer: @UUID[Item.tG5i6sJgib1ZaE8y]{Marasoda, the Sludge Slayer}

  • Cube: Extremely corrosive. Anyone reaching into it takes [[/r 1d6]] damage.

  • Runes: Anyone with a magical background will recognize that these are harmless but extremely vulgar insults and curses against ooze-fighting hero of legend, Domhnall O’Dunn.

The Aftermath.name: The Aftermath
The Aftermath.text:
If the PCs escape through the drain in @UUID[.E10dIyCTD8CnW8IL]{Area 4} or cave in @UUID[.OlHSrCg85LxqRsCS]{Area 17} they are not pursued and are free to live their lives or perhaps seek revenge on the cult. Most importantly, they gain their first level and become adventurers with a built-in, slime-centric backstory.

If the PCs escape through the doors in @UUID[.oolOfQ1kFLuwCLuX]{Area 15}. They are greeted by a crowd of two dozen or so ooze cultists, disfigured and grim. Many have melted faces and some have hands or feet that have been dissolved to the bone. All are silent save one, who pronounces the @UUID[Item.mVZaPPZt05Om1eGu]{Boon of the Slime Lord} on each survivor. The PCs are allowed to leave, and also gain their first level as well as the harrowing tale of how they earned it.

Area 17: The Passage.name: Area 17: The Passage
Area 17: The Passage.text:
The tunnel is trapped. A short passage dug through rock and dirt leads to a large cavern. Four @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.FzBj2e0DzIjvQ0JE]{wolves} gnaw on bones or rest their hoary heads on their paws. Daylight pours through the passage to the west.

  • Trapped: A thin wire stretches across the midpoint of the tunnel. If it is tripped, the tunnel collapses and anyone inside takes [[/r 1d4]] damage and suffocates within 1 round.

  • Wolves: Attack anyone passing through. Attempts to sneak past are made at disadvantage due to their keen senses.

Random Encounters.name: Random Encounters

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Early this morning, cultist of the Crimson Hand raided the nearby village of Hillshire, capturing several villagers before disappearing into the night.

Sister Inna, a priestess of St. Terragnis who escaped the attack, hopes to enlist the PCs in rescuing the villagers, especially @UUID[Actor.81mxXvuC4Eri44bF]{Father Marcus} (a pillar of the community), saying they can keep any of the chapel's treasure recovered from the raiders.

If the PCs pursue the cultists, they can easily track them to their lair, a dark temple carved into the side of a mountain.

The cultists are led by @UUID[Actor.6VWM6Wb47guFI4p4]{Dark Apostle Moloch}, a dangerous and charismatic man, who seeks to bolster his forces by "converting" the strong (through sinister, mind-controlling magic), and sacrificing the rest to his dark god, Ramlaat the Pillager.


CULT DETAILS

Crimson Hand. The Cult seeks the favor of Ramlaat to grow in power before a prophesized apocalypse where only the strongest will survive.

Core Cult Tenants.

  • Honor Ramlaat and his Skull Altars with blood.

  • Obey until you can usurp.

  • Only the strong survive.

Cult Ranks. Strict hierarchy, denoted by robe color:

  1. 1 Cult Leader (Black Robe with Gold Trim). Apostle Moloch

  2. 2 Masters (Black Robes). Master-at-Arms and Mistress of Pain

  3. ~12 Acolytes/Hunters (Red Robes). Not allowed in Moloch's Chambers

  4. ~24 Neophytes (Brown Robes). Not allowed east of Great Hall

If PCs disguised as cultists, typically not questioned by cultists of equal or lower rank (unless acting suspicious).

CULTIST TEMPLE

Light. Illuminated unless noted. Only @UUID[Actor.6VWM6Wb47guFI4p4]{Apostle Moloch} and @UUID[Actor.fh3tkPui9VD7I4kF]{Mistress of Pain} are dark-adapted

Danger Level. Unsafe. Check every 3 rounds or after loud noises. D6 roll of 1 = encounter.

Escaped villager and… (roll again, reroll 5+)

Special Rules.name: Special Rules
Special Rules.text:
Rescue the Villagers.

  • PCs gain 1 XP per villager rescued (2 XP for Father Marcus)

  • If clear path to exit, can escape without escort.

Blood Lust.

  • When afflicted, use next action to attack the nearest creature (with ADV), or take 1d4 damage.

DIFFICULTY SCALING

These optional rules can be used for difficulty scaling.

Fate Worse Than Death.

  • Cultist do non-lethal damage unless noted. "Take them alive!"

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
BACKGROUND

Years ago, an eccentric nobleman grew bored of his frivolous, hedonistic lifestyle. To satiate his nefarious thoughts, he used his immense wealth to purchase the Diabolical Lair from a gold dragon. The nobleman retrofitted the lair to conduct dastardly experiments, which led him to discover a new purpose: to create as much chaos as possible. Combining his love of science while honoring the first manifestation of chaos, he took on a new moniker, Professor Memnon.

FACTIONS

@UUID[Actor.hz7tggbkC9xtHX3n]{Professor Memnon}. Callous Megalomaniac. Loves to test his chaotic creations on the unsuspecting. Believes his diabolical lair is impervious.

@UUID[Actor.4KXEJGg63d4FctWW]{Red Maned Kobolds}. Subservient and Crafty. Included in the sale of the lair. Forced to wear red manes. They maintain and improve the diabolical traps. May hold disdain for their new boss.

@UUID[Actor.TOQT7tcNE0JN4lcG]{Nestor} the Legless Giant. Loyal and Dimwitted. Professor Memnon’s bodyguard. Adept at climbing and swinging, can traverse lair with ease.

@UUID[Actor.dUp16fdIVoJdaHFl]{Eunice} the Psychic Jellyfish. Deceitful and Cruel. Eunice devoured her children to absorb their power. Professor Memnon built her a robotic frame so she can freely roam the lair.

THE DIABOLICAL LAIR

The Diabolical Lair is a secure location carved into a mountain close to a nearby town. Unless otherwise stated, the walls and doors are made from carved stone & the ceilings are 15ft high.

Entrances and Exits. Carved steps pass through the mouth of an enormous stone lion and lead to @UUID[.kQOeIzaGH1bPwAaJ]{ Area 1} the entrance hall. It is possible, yet treacherous, to climb up the waterfall to @UUID[.PDM11MCYqk84cytY]{Area 6} (4:6 chance the @UUID[Actor.KOvytBf5KJdazLtA]{Harpy} is in her nest).

Danger Level. Risky. 1:6 chance for a random encounter every 2 crawling rounds or when the PCs make noise or activate a weird device

MAKE IT YOURS

This adventure can be run as a one shot, or inserted into an existing campaign. Professor Memnon’s identity is depicted as a nameless noble, but he should be linked to the PCs: an odd patron, friendly mayor, or estranged relative. It is recommended to play this module using Pulp Mode (SD p.111).

RUMORS

d6

Rumor

Truth

1

Birds have been acting strangely, falling from the sky, their wings singed and eyes dissolved.

Half-True

2

The Diabolical Lair was purchased from a Gold Dragon, and she was forced to relocate her hoard.

True

3

He often collaborates with other villains: Ramlaat’s Raider and Seductress Shune. They are forming a villainous super league.

False

4

A local musician bragged about carousing with a Legless Giant and a Rust Monster. He has not been seen for months.

True

5

The Professor utilizes artifice, harnessing the elements to power his dastardly experiments.

True

6

Ritual sacrifice is being performed in the Diabolic Lair in an attempt to summon a deity.

False

If the players are able to defeat Professor Memnon they can obtain the following:

  • @UUID[Item.xW3V656hDFKmslru]{Memnon’s Mask}. When worn, people magically forget your true identity.

Back Page.name: Back Page
Back Page.text:
INSPIRATION

This pulp funhouse dungeon draws inspiration from Doctor Satan, written by Paul Ernst. In these novelette’s, Doctor Satan is a rich man who obsesses over the occult and strange experiments. He uses his resources to become the “world's weirdest criminal”. He is assisted by a legless giant named Bostiff, a direct inspiration for Nestor. I have also included numerous easter eggs that reference Doctor Satan’s vile experiments, as well as some subtle nods to the other assigned covers, Thing of Darkness & John Cawder’s Wife.

- ERSK

A terrible storm is brewing – you must find shelter from this accursed weather, and quickly! Area 1: Empty Hallway.name: Area 1: Empty Hallway
Area 1: Empty Hallway.text:
• Wind howls through the cracks in the stone walls.

  • Chandelier is hanging from one of the beams. Pigeons have built a nest on it.

  • Debris and wooden beams on the ground.

  • Firewood and broken crates lie stacked against the wall. There is a wood-chopping axe leaning by the door to @UUID[.bvxmidCgjlPqhx9d]{Area 2}.

  • Voices can be heard from the Area 2, DC 11 to hear two people arguing who’s turn it is feed the hounds downstairs.

  • Stone stairs lead directly to @UUID[.tmHJS0tRpu0TIHVk]{Area 10}. Anyone climbing the stairs may alert sentries above. Loose stones make noise, DC 11 to pass undetected.

@UUID[Macro.cXQ9S5xGUfUxM8N0]{Reveal Area 1+2}

Area 2: Storage Room.name: Area 2: Storage Room
Area 2: Storage Room.text:
• Barrels and crates are piled up all around the room. They provide some cover. The crates are mostly empty, the rest are full of stolen goods (200 gp but really heavy).

  • A pulley system hangs above the large open trapdoor. Long chain hangs down the hatch leading to @UUID[.np2baXNQjXueMReA]{Area 7}.

  • Two @UUID[Actor.ry0N3R6hXcfJJ0Lv]{nasty-looking ruffians} are yelling at each other, arguing, while the third one enjoys the show. They can be surprised, but will attack the party on sight otherwise.

@UUID[Macro.cXQ9S5xGUfUxM8N0]{Reveal Area 1+2}

Area 3: Magically Locked Room.name: Area 3: Magically Locked Room
Area 3: Magically Locked Room.text:
• The door to this room is locked with a seal, can be smashed with DC 17, but will make a loud noise and alert everyone in the fort. Opens with a special key located in @UUID[.UZHErFFniq0BzLzn]{Area 12}.

  • Rotten tapestries display knights and kings jousting. There is a wooden chair and a table. If touched, all crumbles to dust.

  • Heavy iron chest is pinned underneath fallen stone blocks. Can be pulled out with DC 10. Contains a golden statuette of a young woman (50 gp), plated silver gloves, and a @UUID[Item.EyS2PAd9l6bLuW1a]{magic longsword}. If the statuette is taken, a ghost of a sad woman will appear in the room, somberly looking at the door. The ghost is silent and harmless but will permanently reduce CON by [[/r 1d8]] points to anyone who breaks the statuette. This is the ghost of a skeleton in the @UUID[.ixcJq6DNfCXGJeOu]{Area 8}.

  • Reinforced wooden trapdoor leads to @UUID[.ixcJq6DNfCXGJeOu]{Area 8}. The door was locked once, but now, the mechanism is rusty and broken beyond repair.

@UUID[Macro.RTU8YHH15jEALEqv]{Reveal Area 3}

Area 4: Atrium.name: Area 4: Atrium
Area 4: Atrium.text:
• The southern door of this room is unlocked, but closed and reinforced with iron bars.

  • Beautiful frescoes are still visible on the walls, displaying a knight and a lady in love, riding a winged horse.

  • Shallow fountian full of buzzing flies and mosquitoes reeks of stale sewage. If searched (DC 13), a silver ring (10 gp) can be found at the bottom.

  • Grey stormy skies can be seen from below. The first raindrops are already here.

  • The eastern door is missing from the hinges, the busy interior of @UUID[.VtLjQm8kYPJ4NyBy]{Area 5} can be seen from here.

@UUID[Macro.dPYPPw44ObNwcDXY]{Reveal Area 4+5}

Area 5: Sleeping Chambers.name: Area 5: Sleeping Chambers
Area 5: Sleeping Chambers.text:
• Bright orange flame illuminates the room as three @UUID[Actor.ry0N3R6hXcfJJ0Lv]{bandits} huddled together next to a fireplace, play card games and rolling dice. Surprisingly, they are quiet, trying their best not to wake up their sleeping comrades.

  • Big iron bell is next to the gambling bandits. If the bandits notice the characters, they will ring the bell and alert all the bandits in the fort. The bell is very old, intricately engraved, and was stolen months ago, it is worth 10 gp, or 100 gp if sold to the right buyer.

  • Seven bunkbeds are in this room. Two bunkbeds have occupants - four sleeping bandits.

  • Large and empty king-sized bed is next to the ladder leading to @UUID[.rHhUVHhmUFRXYSvZ]{Area 11}. There is a @UUID[Item.seWGReDDSkaKffvl]{dagger +1} hidden under its dirty pillows.

  • Two chests are by the large bed. The smaller one is unlocked and looks empty. It has a hidden compartment, DC 15 to notice it. Inside is a magic @UUID[Item.wErvoBzzV5xMaG3m]{Scroll of Speak with Dead} and a strange locket. The locket shows a portrait of someone you wish to remember. Currently, it holds an image of a five year old girl. The large chest is locked, DC 13 to unlock. It contains a variety of coins and jewelry (150 gp).

  • Trapdoor on the ceiling of this room is locked, DC 13 to open. The trapdoor leads to @UUID[.rHhUVHhmUFRXYSvZ]{Area 11}.

@UUID[Macro.dPYPPw44ObNwcDXY]{Reveal Area 4+5}

Area 6: Den of Wolves.name: Area 6: Den of Wolves
Area 6: Den of Wolves.text:
• The ground is muddy and sticky. Movement is difficult, DC 10 or get stuck in the mud. Spend an action to pull yourself out.

  • Snarls can be heard in the darkness. Two @UUID[Actor.b0kmgW3NFVkmMeA7]{wolves} are poised to strike! They will attack any character carrying a torch.

  • Malodorous pond is on the western part of the cavern and the way leads to @UUID[.aCJWSl7XWHmPy11V]{Area 8}, but the stones have caved in and it is impossible to go through unless the rocks are cleared. It takes an hour to clear.

  • There is a corpse of a middle-aged human floating in the pond. The corpse is bloated and full of leeches and flesh-eating snails. If inspected, the corpse will reveal an unreadable soaked letter, and a children’s silver bracelet (10 gp) in the envelope.

  • Hidden door on the north wall! Touching the cave walls reveals a faux rock - painted surprisingly well, DC 13 to notice. The door leads to @UUID[.np2baXNQjXueMReA]{Area 7}.

@UUID[Macro.frnguPzv0a9iYwlS]{Reveal Area 6}

Area 7: Old Wine Cellar.name: Area 7: Old Wine Cellar
Area 7: Old Wine Cellar.text:
• Smell of mold and vinegar wafts through the room. Broken bottles lie all around the corners. There is a 2-in-6 chance that a bottle of old elven vintage worth 15 gp is still intact. Tastes great!

  • Big cluster of mushrooms on the ceiling illuminates the room in vibrant hues of blue and purple.

  • Four thick wooden beams hold the ceiling in place. They are a new addition to this room. If at least two of the beams are broken or removed in some way, the ceiling will collapse and kill everyone in the room.

  • Rusty steel ladder bolted in the wall leads to @UUID[.bvxmidCgjlPqhx9d]{Area 2}.

@UUID[Macro.ydmghxCQB5X3r7pv]{Reveal Area 7}

Area 8: Ruined Dungeon.name: Area 8: Ruined Dungeon
Area 8: Ruined Dungeon.text:
• Damp and slippery. Everything is covered by a layer of slime and hundreds upon hundreds of fat slugs. Step on them, they pop!

  • Chains and manacles are bolted into dungeon walls. Moldy skeletons are attached to some of them.

  • Human skeleton lies on the floor, adorned in rotting court dress, with dirty pieces of jewelry (30 gp) still attached to it. Bones of the skeleton appear to be broken, as if it was thrown from above. This is the skeleton of a ghost in the @UUID[.j3rnEtiH1zcaYTxV]{Area 3}.

  • Rickety ladder made of wood is swarmed by slugs. The wood is rotten, and climbing the ladder takes some effort, DC 9. The ladder leads to @UUID[.j3rnEtiH1zcaYTxV]{Area 3}.

  • Three fat @UUID[Actor.aQa0g6rrazakogL9]{giant rats} are living in this room, feeding off of slugs. They are well fed and will not attack, unless provoked.

@UUID[Macro.IjRL5CnhEuQ28X4X]{Reveal Area 8}

Area 9: Crumbling Wall.name: Area 9: Crumbling Wall
Area 9: Crumbling Wall.text:
• The storm is getting closer. The wind begins to rage. It is not safe outside anymore.

  • Ground is littered with broken stones and stone slabs. Movement is noisy, and a bit difficult, but not impossible.

  • Sturdy reinforced door to the east leads to @UUID[.tmHJS0tRpu0TIHVk]{Area 10}. The door is barred from the inside, DC 17 to force open.

  • Broken door to the north leads to @UUID[.UZHErFFniq0BzLzn]{Area 12}. “Do not enter!” is written on one of the planks. @UUID[Macro.Ez9UktmBz5aJKSd8]{Display Door Sign}

Area 10: Sentry Room.name: Area 10: Sentry Room
Area 10: Sentry Room.text:
• Two @UUID[Actor.ry0N3R6hXcfJJ0Lv]{bandits} and their sergeant guard the wall section from this small chamber. There is 2-in-6 chance that the bandits are currently looking through the door, making it impossible for anyone to pass through @UUID[.xSlMyvtRLzs0Jh8j]{Area 9} undetected for [[/r 3d10]] minutes.

  • Three sleeping bags are placed around a bonfire. There is a pouch of gold (10 gp) and a throwing @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.C3mc5OlKPSJNMrng]{dagger} in one of the bags.

  • Stairway on the south leads to @UUID[.sBfbdldBV24BZ5a1]{Area 1}.

@UUID[Macro.jWVzO07WFic42sV0]{Reveal Area 10}

Area 11: Old Armory.name: Area 11: Old Armory
Area 11: Old Armory.text:
• Half of the roof is missing. Beams are broken and most shingles are gone. Pigeons nest here now.

  • Weapon racks and armor stands lay empty, piled up against the north wall.

  • Heavy iron door to the west is busted open and bent, unable to close again, leading to @UUID[.UZHErFFniq0BzLzn]{Area 12}. The weight of stones and beams appears to be the culprit.

  • Fresh corpse of a man dressed in green robes lies next to two dead stingbats, both cut in half. His body is full of stingbat punctures, not a single drop of blood left in it. He clutches a silver dagger +1 and a @UUID[.2LLiIJVKJSgxbNQt]{journal}. The robed man also wears an old ruby ring (15 gp) and a silk pouch with gems (30 gp). In his pocket is a pair of keys, one opens the large chest in @UUID[.VtLjQm8kYPJ4NyBy]{Area 5}, the other is for the trapdoor in this room.

  • Trapdoor on the south-eastern corner of this room is locked, DC 13 to open. The trapdoor leads to @UUID[.VtLjQm8kYPJ4NyBy]{Area 5}.

@UUID[Macro.q463B9B3G48qlqjn]{Reveal Area 11}

Area 12: Grimhill Tower.name: Area 12: Grimhill Tower
Area 12: Grimhill Tower.text:
• The tower has collapsed from the inside, only the moss-covered walls still stand.

  • A sudden flash of lightning illuminates the place, revealing four @UUID[Actor.Mk3OW3RSgGNSkcuC]{stingbats} hanging from the support beams. They attack!

  • Armored knight lies dead in the rubble. The knight wears rusty platemail and a shield with a crest lost to time. Next to the knight is a locked chest, DC 17. Inside it are a golden statuette of a young man (50 gp), a long emerald necklace (70 gp), and a jeweled crown (150 gp). If the characters attempt to open the chest or interfere with it in some way, the knight will rise as a @UUID[Actor.vOHaLShvVtwFfEfY]{wight} and attack. The wight has a special key to @UUID[.j3rnEtiH1zcaYTxV]{Area 3} attached to its belt.

  • Iron door to the east leads to @UUID[.rHhUVHhmUFRXYSvZ]{Area 11}.

  • Broken door to the south leads to @UUID[.xSlMyvtRLzs0Jh8j]{Area 9}.

A: Main Entrance.name: A: Main Entrance
A: Main Entrance.text:
• Wooden signpost that says “You are not welcome here!”. @UUID[Macro.QahTnsu8DxLH8X6F]{Display Signpost}

  • A gust of wind knocks a few branches and pebbles from the ruined walls above.

  • Sturdy oaken door, slightly ajar, squeaks loudly if not opened with caution, DC 9.

B: Hidden Cave.name: B: Hidden Cave
B: Hidden Cave.text:
• Faint stench of wet dogs permeates the air. Not even the smell of fresh rain can hide it.

  • The cave entrance is hidden by branches and tall grass. It can be seen from the road, DC 13.

  • There are bones littered around the entrance. Mostly animal, but some are certainly human.

@UUID[Macro.OqbpswnpOTt5DpIl]{Reveal Hidden Cave Enterance}

C: Wall Vines.name: C: Wall Vines
C: Wall Vines.text:
• Broken wall overgrown in vines is somewhat challenging to climb, DC 13. Failure by five or more will loosen some of the stones which will deal [[/r 1d4]] damage to the closest person below, DC 9 for half damage. Once the loose stones fall, the vines will be much easier to climb, DC 9.

  • Some vines have thorns that deal one point of damage to anyone without gloves. There are old blood stains on the vines.

  • Oddly beautiful skull shaped white roses grow on the vines. They smell of sorrow.

Reuniting the Tragic Lovers.name: Reuniting the Tragic Lovers
Reuniting the Tragic Lovers.text: If the characters discover both golden statuettes (from @UUID[.j3rnEtiH1zcaYTxV]{Area 3} and @UUID[.UZHErFFniq0BzLzn]{Area 12}), they will notice that the statues fit together perfectly. If the statuettes are reunited, the ghost in @UUID[.j3rnEtiH1zcaYTxV]{Area 3} will vanish, and the wight in @UUID[.UZHErFFniq0BzLzn]{Area 12} will turn to dust, and the words “Glad to see you again, my love...“ will echo in the wind. @UUID[Macro.Yps87krKC1XMf4uf]{Display Echo in the Wind}. All of a sudden, the storm will subside, the rain stop, and the sky will turn blue once more.

Osgarl's Journal.name: Osgarl's Journal
Osgarl's Journal.text:
If the characters decide to take some time to read the journal, they will find boring notes about stolen goods and how the spoils were being divided. They will also learn about the gang’s hierarchy. Osgarl the magician is the bandit leader, while Bert the sergeant is his second in command.

In his journal, Osgarl also mentions that he has chosen Grimhill Fort as the base of his operations because the place has quite the unique history. He mentions undying love and tragic and unfortunate imprisonment of a noblewoman, and murderous rivalry between two knights - two brothers.

In his research, Osgarl has discovered that the unexplored stringbat-infested tower hides intriguing treasures. He also addresses their value and his unwillingness to share with Bert and his crew. This is why Osgarl wanted to delve in all by himself, until his sudden and untimely death.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
ADVENTURE BACKGROUND

Beneath a colossal tree of golden leaves lies a maze of root-choked catacombs. It is in these catacombs that the Dusk Queen of legend is entombed with her royal treasures. However, deathless guardians and devious tricks await any who would intrude on her sleep…

CHARACTER LEVEL

Tomb of the Dusk Queen is a simple but deadly dungeon delve designed for 1st-level characters.

DANGER LEVEL

Unsafe. Check every 3 crawling rounds for random encounters.

Rumors

d6

Rumor

1

A young woman claiming to be the great-granddaughter of the Dusk Queen went missing in the tomb

2

A false scepter lures thieves to an agonizing death

3

The ghost of an Elvish warrior buried in the tomb haunts those who steal her secret door-detecting sword

4

Those who harvest sacred wheat keep a secret

5

A scroll of fireball in the tomb is cursed to incinerate the caster instead of her targets

6

The gelatinous cube cannot harm someone carrying the Dusk Queen’s holy symbol

Random Encounters.name: Random Encounters
Random Encounters.text:
@UUID[RollTable.wplxUyB193h3zler]{Random Encounters}

Random Encounters

d6

Details

1

[[/r 1d6]] @UUID[Actor.UckXEQ9D5DtFJV6Z]{war-maiden skeletons} rise from rubble and attack

2

Ghost (female elf) of enchanted sword’s original owner appears to reclaim sword—by force if necessary

3

NPC thief (female human) flees from chamber further into Dusk Queen’s tomb—roll reaction as normal

4

@UUID[Actor.X3pPgSkJiqnjdeTo]{Cave creeper} scuttles down from shadowy ceiling

5

Mithril suit of animated armor reforms and attacks

6

Golden roots snake down from ceiling and seal off passageway of GM’s choice for 3 crawling rounds

Area 1: Burial Mound.name: Area 1: Burial Mound
Area 1: Burial Mound.text:
Pillars: Covered in roots from aboveground, sickly yellow flowers bloom from the roots. Burial Mound: Nearly reaches the ceiling.

  • Mound: Disturbing mound causes six @UUID[Actor.UckXEQ9D5DtFJV6Z]{war-maiden skeletons} to rise and attack.

  • Rotted Coffin: Buried in mound. Contains moldering bones, mithril bracelet worth 25 gp, @UUID[Item.5h51TWwyrqZQRqsv]{enchanted mithril longsword}, @UUID[Item.vaujNgBzS6lnwWgO]{scroll of fireball}, @UUID[Item.DvMZXkoXYd2tOc72]{scroll of invisibility}, and @UUID[Item.fiFBFojEGDIgygpV]{full moon guidance stone}.

Area 2: Sealing Corridor.name: Area 2: Sealing Corridor
Area 2: Sealing Corridor.text:
Walls: Sagging and covered in roots.

  • Pressure Plate: Obvious to characters, marked “T” on map. Applying force or weight to pressure plate causes wall to slide shut over area marked “X” on the map.

  • Slow Grinding: Characters triggering trap have time to choose between staying in this area or jumping back to @UUID[.uXtxMjxEj7jlMrBX]{Area 1}.

Area 3: Ruined Idol.name: Area 3: Ruined Idol
Area 3: Ruined Idol.text:
Rubble: Toppled remains of Dusk Queen idol. Centipedes: Pick at smaller vermin in rubble. Broken Down Wall: Leads north into cave.

  • Mold-Covered Portcullis: Rusted shut and covered in yellow mold. Characters can see @UUID[.oyuYcs0q4rcvAlFB]{Area 6} beyond. Characters disturbing or burning mold must roll DC 21 CON or die after 1 crawling round.

Area 4: Twilight Grotto.name: Area 4: Twilight Grotto
Area 4: Twilight Grotto.text:
Twilight: Falls in dim shafts through cracks in ceiling. Bones and Feathers: Carpet ground. Silver Chest: In center of grotto.

  • Owlbear Zombie: Lairs in cave and attacks.

  • Halfling Youth: Appear on round 2, throw rocks at characters, owlbear, or both.

  • Open Chest: Contains shiny stones, bird eggs, trinkets worth 10 gp, and mud-caked @UUID[Item.bHhAdAN27LODHVgD]{holy symbol} bearing image of golden tree.

Area 5: Heroine's Tomb.name: Area 5: Heroine's Tomb
Area 5: Heroine's Tomb.text:
Murals: Depicts Elvish warrior-woman in scale armor riding basilisk into battle. Ceiling: Dark, high. Sarcophagus: Atop tier, polished.

  • Search for Traps: Mithril arrowheads scattered across ground. No apparent trap on exterior of sarcophagus.

  • Open Sarcophagus: Heavy, requires combined STR of 30. Magnetic arrows fire from dark ceiling high above at all in chamber. DC 15 DEX or [[/r 1d4]] damage and magnetic arrowheads embedded in flesh until end of adventure.

  • Look In Sarcophagus: Empty. Hidden crawl at bottom to @UUID[.oyuYcs0q4rcvAlFB]{Area 6}.

  • Magnetic Arrowheads: If lightning bolt cast in presence of character with magnetic arrowheads embedded in flesh, 50% chance bolt will target them instead.

Area 6: Obelisk and Scepter.name: Area 6: Obelisk and Scepter
Area 6: Obelisk and Scepter.text:
Obelisk: Preserved body of Elvish warrior woman in scale armor stands within obelisk. She holds scepter and wears scarab.

  • Reach into Obelisk: Blades scythe across opening, +5 to hit, [[/r 2d6]] damage. If reduced to 0 hp, hands severed and scuttle away through cracks in walls. Will return later at inopportune time (GM’s discretion) to steal item character is about to use.

  • Search for Traps: Withered and greedy severed hands in dirt in front of body. DC 18 DEX to disable blades; failure triggers attack.

  • Treasure: @UUID[Item.rFCggBwpZLW3qho8]{Scepter of the Dusk Queen}, @UUID[Item.vOoglypNSycIC2PM]{scarab of drain resistance}, and mithril signet ring worth 50 gp.

Area 7: Scoured Passageway.name: Area 7: Scoured Passageway
Area 7: Scoured Passageway.text:
Corridor: Narrow with moist walls. Remarkably free of debris. Skeleton: Human, appears to float halfway down passageway.

  • Gelatinous Cube: Lurks invisible in middle of passageway.

  • Keepsake: @UUID[Item.MUT6HBfvFpIJrIda]{Locket} on skeleton inside gelatinous cube. Contains painted portrait of young human male and Elvish woman. If returned to Morwen, she rewards them with Elvish word to activate random utility item on her corpse in @UUID[.BZrjtGwN3RvEKODD]{Area 8} —“vála.”

Area 8: Hall of Plaster.name: Area 8: Hall of Plaster
Area 8: Hall of Plaster.text:
Ceilings: High and vaulted. Braziers: Cast iron, cage-like, hang at 10’ intervals from ceiling. Walls: Covered in plaster murals depicting women harvesting wheat by light of colossal golden tree. Sound: Faint sound of women singing harvest hymns.

  • Secret Door: Behind image of Dusk Queen painted in mural. Opened by pressing stone button in crown. Found by explicitly searching queen’s image, wielding secret door-detecting sword, or heeding rumor about women who harvest wheat.

  • Collapsed Stairway: Through archway in southeast wall. Ghost of Morwen lingers 30’ down above her broken and buried corpse.

  • Morwen, Descendent of Dusk Queen. Young female elf thief. Laments she did not perish in sight of her love. Random utility magic item on corpse, offers activation word if characters bring her keepsake of her beloved. Also has @UUID[Item.UTm56Ip6J7N1f3LY]{fragile silver spear}.

  • Dimension Door: Green misty portal leading to @UUID[.uoQ0cBS9RbAcvEye]{Area 13}. Cast by Morwen using scroll. She has knowledge of area 13’s layout.

Area 9: False Crown.name: Area 9: False Crown
Area 9: False Crown.text:
Walls: Rounded, decorated with mithril plates depicting Dusk Queen on her throne. Ceiling: High above, crescent moon-shaped opening. Moonlight: Shines on crown on pedestal. Smell: Spoiled meat.

  • @UUID[Actor.X3pPgSkJiqnjdeTo]{Cave Creepers}: Mated pair ambush characters entering chamber.

  • Inspect Crown Up Close: A fake—it’s rotted wood painted gold.

Area 10: Enchanted Mosaic.name: Area 10: Enchanted Mosaic
Area 10: Enchanted Mosaic.text:
Walls: Mosaic of painted stones depicting robed woman facing mountain peaks, raising her arms in jubilation toward colossal crescent moon rising above horizon.

  • Oracle of Dusk: If mosaic is touched, stones rearrange themselves to show robed woman beckoning characters. She identifies herself as Oracle of Dusk and offers to truthfully answer one “yes-or-no” question about dungeon.

Area 11: Bonfire.name: Area 11: Bonfire
Area 11: Bonfire.text:
Cave: Cramped, damp, mossy. Bonfire: Some kindling remains.

  • Light Bonfire. Once per adventure, restores all hit points and expended spells. Must be lit and used as group.

  • Roleplaying. Ask each character what they are thinking about while resting in silence around crackling fire.

Area 12: Charnel Basilisk.name: Area 12: Charnel Basilisk
Area 12: Charnel Basilisk.text:
Stalagmites and Stalactites: Dot chamber like fangs of some great behemoth. Rainwater: Runs down in rivulets from ceiling. Urns: Overflowing piles eroding in rainwater puddles. Smell: Reeks of lizard and rotten eggs. Sound: Crunching rock.

  • Spilled Urns: Wedding bands worth 25 gp and matched pair of @UUID[Item.WiywC1GAgYVc47Og]{rings of protection}. Elvish marriage vows engraved on both rings.

  • @UUID[Actor.L1ImzZ1ViXiCsUEi]{Basilisk}: Devours stone urns, defends nest.

  • Search Urns: If searching after defeating basilisk, characters find @UUID[Item.k6fmUalbbLPxcbew]{Crown of the Dusk Queen}. Searching during battle takes an action, 1-in-6 chance of finding crown.

Area 13: Royal Hall.name: Area 13: Royal Hall
Area 13: Royal Hall.text:
Statues: Armored Elvish women holding up holy symbols debossed with moon and colossal tree symbols. Double Doors: Sealed, no handles, engraved with stylized colossal tree and mourning Elvish women. Smell: Baking cinnamon.

  • Dimension Door: Created by Morwen, leads back to @UUID[.BZrjtGwN3RvEKODD]{Area 8}.

  • Sealed Door: Raise holy symbol found in @UUID[.l6NTkkDdcDxmkS5h]{Area 4} to open doors.

  • Trap: Attempting to open doors without first raising holy symbol from @UUID[.l6NTkkDdcDxmkS5h]{Area 4} causes images of burning great tree to cover doors. Heat swells. Each character must roll DC 18 CON or take [[/r 1d6]] damage per active light source. Fell wind puts out flames and extinguishes all light sources afterward.

Area 14: Grand Tomb of Dusk.name: Area 14: Grand Tomb of Dusk
Area 14: Grand Tomb of Dusk.text:
Ceiling: Stretches into gloom above. Columns: Massive, round, covered in shifting roots thick as sea serpents. Roots: Glow from within with golden light that pulses like heartbeat, motes flit like fireflies between roots.

  • Well: Filled with brackish water, 20’ deep. Rusted iron door at bottom of well is locked. Darkness and water pressure makes lock picking extremely difficult (DC 24).

  • Throne: Chiseled from coal-colored marble. Dusk Queen statue sits 10’ tall on throne, missing crown and scepter. Half-moon tapestries frame her artfully sculpted flowing hair and stern gaze.

  • Replace Scepter and Crown: Throne retracts to reveal Dusk Queen’s sarcophagus beneath. Chiseled from onyx and glitters with first stars of twilight.

  • Open Sarcophagus: Contains exquisite jewelry worth 600 gp, @UUID[Item.Efexs9CWhVdSAEWE]{potion of extra-healing}, @UUID[Item.IYru7iUYu0KbwjyE]{scroll of lightning bolt}, and @UUID[Item.ILvO0olsj4nW6r0l]{well-gaol key}. Also contains Dusk Queen mummy, who rises and attacks.

Taunts from the Dusk Queen

@UUID[Macro.4GbTGBzBbNkMaEWO]{Rise from Sarcophagus Taunt}

@UUID[Macro.rWXA5G5BF6YZTggV]{Life Drain Taunt}

@UUID[Macro.3D9atKbAoq2OUvgq]{Charm Taunt}

@UUID[Macro.3IxV5cneraqOZMwo]{Mirror Image Taunt}

@UUID[Macro.1dBndwNEYGaQoNrS]{Sticks to Snakes Taunt}

Ending the Adventure.name: Ending the Adventure
Ending the Adventure.text:
The Dusk Queen’s scepter and crown fetch 300 gp if sold as a pair.

The locked steel door at the bottom of the well can be opened with the well-gaol key found in the Dusk Queen’s sarcophagus.

Doing so causes the water in the well to drain away, rushing down a flight of spiral steps deeper into the mysterious underworld beneath the colossal golden tree…

[3] The Awful Amber Doom.description:
The ancient scrolls tell the tale of bright Elysium, beacon of virtue, and its fall into the worship of Rhedon, demon-god of the sea.

As punishment, one calamitous solstice night, the gods abandoned the city and let the cold waters swallow it up.

Rhedon is long dead, and now, on the eve of the century solstice, the anniversary of its fall, the moon glows amber and the City Beneath the Sea rises up from its salty grave for one cursed night.

Your arch-foe, the Corpse-Master, races through the ruins, seeking the fabled Cranberry Goblet, an artifact of legendary power, said to be hidden somewhere in the city.

You must stop him, lest his powers be increased a hundredfold. Overcome the dangers of the city, find the goblet, and stop the Corpse-Master and his lackeys once and for all, before twelve hours pass and the city drowns again with the dawn.

Inspiration.name: Inspiration
Inspiration.text:
PROMPTS

The Cranberry Goblet - Jan 1946

The City from the Sea - May 1940

The Corpse-Master - July 1925

CONCEPTION

We were thrilled to have drawn three such inspirational covers. The Corpse-Master from July 1925 immediately struck us as a perfect name for a pulp villain, & the ghostly priestess & ragged man there seemed useful, too.

The floating skull & skeletal hands from Jan 1946 looked just like the sort of wicked apparition that a guy called “The Corpse-Master” might summon, & of course, the Cranberry Goblet seemed like a perfect Mac-Guffin.

The cover of the May 1940 issue also seemed tailor-made for adventure fodder - a lost city beneath the sea, a giant bat-monster, a couple of small savage humanoids, and a large snake.

We also included elements from the text on the covers, both titles and blurbs. “Awful Amber Doom” became the name for the adventure and the explanation for why the city sank in the first place, and “Lost Elysium” seemed a fine name for the city itself.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
The ancient scrolls tell the tale of bright Elysium, beacon of virtue, and its fall into the worship of Rhedon, demon-god of the sea.

As punishment, one calamitous solstice night, the gods abandoned the city and let the cold waters swallow it up.

Rhedon is long dead, and now, on the eve of the century solstice, the anniversary of its fall, the moon glows amber and the City Beneath the Sea rises up from its salty grave for one cursed night.

Your arch-foe, the Corpse-Master, races through the ruins, seeking the fabled Cranberry Goblet, an artifact of legendary power, said to be hidden somewhere in the city.

You must stop him, lest his powers be increased a hundredfold. Overcome the dangers of the city, find the goblet, and stop the Corpse-Master and his lackeys once and for all, before twelve hours pass and the city drowns again with the dawn.

The NPCs

@UUID[Actor.QmzldZ2KcCi54SxP]{THE CORPSE-MASTER}

Once a mortal man, dark experiments and darker magicks have twisted him into something much like a Vampire.

  • Tactics. The Corpse-Master has entered the city, carried on a palanquin by several dozen @UUID[Actor.uuXvsUBs3XAwvMOA]{Homonculytes}. The tumultuous waters have washed away his trail, and he will remain discrete as long as possible. His Sightless Seekers will scout the path ahead; he and his minions will follow. Once he reaches the Outer Precincts, he will thoroughly search each building, attempting to bend any undead he finds to his will. He may send any new recruits to harass the heroes (or other potential threats) that his Seekers discover. Once he arrives at the Ziggurat, he will proceed directly to its peak to retrieve the Goblet.

  • Agenda. A glutton both in life and undeath, he sees the City Beneath the Sea as a rich source of materiel for his experiments and thinks the Cranberry Goblet may be the key to perfecting his vile creations.

@UUID[Actor.JJiW3zVuaFb3X4Re]{THE ORACLE OF THE MOON}

Eternally bound to the place of her demise, she wanders the streets as a powerful but incorporeal spirit of vengeance.

  • Tactics. The Oracle will put to sleep any intruders that are damaging the city, and can command any living statues. Heroes who speak an ancient language may be able to convince her of their good intentions. Clerics of evil deities or those who consort with demons will be attacked on sight.

  • Agenda. She will do all in her power to protect the City.

@UUID[Actor.X0lmnAYYEkAtPpt2]{PTEOR, THE EXPLORER}

Tall gaunt man with a bushy beard and unkempt hair. The Amber Amulet glistens on his chest, matching the glint in his maddened eyes.

  • Tactics. Pteor will avoid any physical confrontation. If pushed too far or attacked, Pteor will flee.

  • Agenda. During his brief intervals of humanity, Pteor dons whatever rags he can find and wanders the city. He remembers nothing of his former life, except that it was full of adventure and derring-do. All of the inhabitants of the city, supernatural and otherwise, avoid him. He will be confused but helpful towards anyone who treats him kindly; he can provide directions, but will flee, screaming, if the moon disappears for more than a few moments.

@UUID[Actor.HOLfJGhbzr7pOUNl]{THE CHILDE OF RHEDON}

A primordial bat-like beast with leathery wings and shadow-veiled fur. Its piercing yellow eyes and frothing fangs smite courage like a thousand swords.

  • Tactics. The Childe of Rhedon will attack any invader, but it is a blunt instrument. Bright lights and loud noises will catch its attention, but once it realizes that enemies are present, it will diligently search. If badly wounded, it will retreat to its lair in the Moon Ziggurat to transform and heal, then transform again to resume the hunt.

  • Agenda. The Childe of Rhedon is bound to protect @UUID[Item.XXh9mLiTeU5biajV]{The Cranberry Goblet} at all costs. It has no will of its own. Such is the way of this curse.

Synopsis.name: Synopsis
Synopsis.text:
The Man Who Loved Planks Synopsis

The Lord of Mad Mansion, Enoch Warren, has been found dead cradling a plank of wood in his arms. He's depicted as an eccentric, middle-aged man with an intense, peculiar obsession with collecting furniture and wooden planks. This fixation seems harmless at first as he owned a lumber business, but gradually reveals a darker side as Enoch becomes increasingly isolated and consumed by his obsession. His life revolves around acquiring and caring for these planks of wood, leading to strange and unsettling behaviors that hint at deeper psychological issues.

Enoch’s secret is that he shut down his lumber business when he fell in love with a dryad. The dryad appeared to him mangled, cut, and disfigured. She was one of the many victims of Enoch’s trade, being turned into timbers and sent across the lands. The slicing, nailing, and bending of the wood planks caused great pain and torture to the dryads, but it never killed their spirits outright. Only fire would set them free, and so Enoch began tracking down chests, cabinets, nightstands, and all the like in order to tear them apart to planks. Using wire and glue he remade trees plank by plank, then burned them to set the dryads free.

You can read the full story here.

This adventure adapts the story with an opportunity for PCs to loot the mansion, finish Enoch’s work, and earn the Oath of the Dryads.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Background

Panic grips the streets as news spreads that Enoch Warren, the notorious "Lord of Mad Mansion," was caught stealing an antique cherry makeup vanity from a local museum. Once a respected lumber magnate, Enoch became a recluse, obsessed with collecting and burning furniture. His madness was largely dismissed until he was spotted carrying a severed arm—believed to belong to a missing girl—as he fled the scene.

Wounded but not caught, Enoch returned to his mansion with the vanity in tow. An angry mob plans to ransack the mansion, and dig up the grounds to find the girl. The museum curator offers the PCs a reward of 750 gp to recover the vanity before the mob destroys the heirloom. (This reward is heavily suggested to be donated back to the museum, and secretly cannot be paid)

Location Details

The mansion windows have had their wooden shutters torn off and are sealed with iron plates from the inside. The adventure begins at nightfall. There is no light unless otherwise noted. Ceilings are 10 ft unless noted. Unsafe.

Rumors

@UUID[RollTable.37pq2gpxTiaASw3h]{Lord of Mad Mansion Rumors}

d6

Rumor

1

He’s been burning all the furniture in that mansion. Every last bit! (P)

2

Enoch used to be a great painter, and had an art studio in his tower. (T)

3

The ghost of his ex-wife cursed him! That’s why he’s gone mad. (P)

4

5

6

Random Encounters

@UUID[RollTable.AvTBHiEAb8h5Djwa]{Lord of Mad Mansion Random Encounters}

d4

Encounter

1

@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.LFx9hb8JlEfGxDaI]{Mimic}: A mimic reveals itself and attacks with surprise.

2

Living Plank: A plank of wood, animated by a trapped dryad spirit, skitters across the floor. It attempts to fly into random PCs' arms. DC 12 DEX or be hit in the chin and knocked out cold. Can be awoken next round.

3

Dryad’s Lament: A mangled dryad spirit appears, mournfully singing a haunting tune. Her song has a magical effect: all PCs must make a DC 12 WIS or be lulled into a trance, becoming immobilized for 1d4 rounds unless they take damage or are shaken awake by another PC.

4

Haunting Whisper: The voice of a female calls out, “Help me… free me…” It echoes from the great hall in Area 7, coming from one of the trees.

After the fourth random encounter, the angry mob arrives in [[/r 1d4+2]] rounds. Announce this to players. 10 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.BviPIbrJao1ubOX1]{knights} and 20 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.V75YwrR126oziTKk]{peasants}, split between @UUID[.YXroFHUvMwfYcShZ]{Area 1} & @UUID[.GKW5jkpj1fzWG8u1]{Area 2}.

Area 1: Front Door.name: Area 1: Front Door
Area 1: Front Door.text:
Large iron door, set of stairs rise 7 ft up. A large pile of ash sits by the door. Torn up and charred books are scattered about the burnt-up lawn.

Ash Pile: 1.5 ft of white ash topped with still smoldering coals. Prodding reveals wire mesh. The ashes smell faintly chemical. Carelessly disturbing or moving through the coals - 1d4 dmg.

Iron Door: Locked. Past-due bills and collections notices glued to the door. Thieves’ tools or DC 18 STR to open.

Area 2: Destroyed Porch.name: Area 2: Destroyed Porch
Area 2: Destroyed Porch.text:
The foundations of what used to be a large porch. Big holes where posts were removed. Older remnants of ash and fire. Scattered planks lie tangled in chicken wire. Poorly glued sheets of tin serve as a door. Door is elevated 7 ft from the ground. Two-story tower rises 60 ft.

Door: PCs need a boost or grappling hook. Makeshift door to Area 3 is unlocked.

Holes: 12 1 ft sq deep holes. Can be covered with planks, ash, and dirt to make pit traps. Boobytrap with spikes and caltrops.

Window: An open window on the northwest side of the tower can be spotted, leading to Area 13. DC 18 DEX to climb without a grappling hook.

Area 3: Library.name: Area 3: Library
Area 3: Library.text:
A 10 ft ladder lies on the floor to @UUID[.GKW5jkpj1fzWG8u1]{Area 2}. A few tall bookshelves stand tall and empty. There are a number of catalogs and papers scattered about. Paper stacks cover a metal table.

Table: Numerous furniture catalogs and Enoch’s notes. They indicate that he has spent considerable time trying to purchase the cherry vanity but was denied. He writes “fine, I’ll steal it so I can make you whole again”. A family tree shows dozens of names, most crossed off. Three names circled at the top – Arethne, Melne, Chryseis. Arethne has a heart by the name.

Area 4: Foyer.name: Area 4: Foyer
Area 4: Foyer.text:
Stone floor caked with bark and wood scraps. Destroyed husks of furniture fill the hall. Enoch Warren can be seen in @UUID[.TlWL8MHj85bqdOOa]{Area 5} resting on the vanity. He has an arrow in his back, a lit lantern on the vanity.

Enoch: Gravely wounded and sobbing. When alerted, addresses PCs with faint breath and begins dousing himself with oil. Attempts to convey his innocence and urges them to finish his mission. “Please, set the last three free, I haven’t been able to finish. Burn me with Arethne…destroy the last things I care for, for them”. Enoch will try to burn himself and the vanity together, but stumbles with his lantern and only lights himself ablaze.

Debris: Broken furniture and bark scraps, move half speed or [[request 9 DEX]] and risk slipping.

Doors: Door to the north is blocked by wire spools. Door to the south is unlocked.

Area 5: Conservatory.name: Area 5: Conservatory
Area 5: Conservatory.text:
Enoch’s burning corpse is next to the cherry vanity, which is badly damaged. A single plank of cherry wood is laid on top of the vanity; it is not from the vanity itself. A dying lantern provides light within near. Moldy couches and tapestries of forests.

Cherry Plank: When a PC interacts with the plank or vanity, the cherry plank temporarily morphs into a woman’s arm, and it points the PCs down the hall to @UUID[.QDtWNbb83FxeJtkW]{Area 7}. It lightly pulls PCs holding it towards the tree to be attached.

Cherry Makeup Vanity: Destroyed into planks with attacks or crowbar.

Stairs: To @UUID[.MRDwjKaMTlDVaI48]{Area 12}. Inspecting railing determines wood banister was torn off the iron.

Area 6: Lavatories.name: Area 6: Lavatories
Area 6: Lavatories.text:
Women’s restroom to the north, men’s to the south. Both have sinks, and a floor-to-ceiling mirror.

Women’s Restroom: Pristine and perfumed. Sponge on stick hangs on the wall next to an ornate peacock sink of stone. Three perfume vials on the sink ledge. Fancy tub holds a pile of clean towels.

Men’s Restroom: Filthy shower. Torn book pages and bills beside the toilet. Ornate stone bull sink. Bull has a nose ring – if tugged, mirror opens to @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}.

Perfume: Charm, 1 use. Your Charisma stat becomes 18 (+4) for [[/r 1d6]] rounds.

Area 7: Great Hall.name: Area 7: Great Hall
Area 7: Great Hall.text:
20ft ceilings. Smells sweet and sticky. Three partially made wire cylinders rise in alcoves across the hall, the westernmost having some branches of bent, pliable wire mesh. Blankets and pillows are found in the raised northern portion of the hall. Three 10 ft ladders by each metal base. Along the middle, remnants of a long banquet table and chairs.

Makeshift Bed: Key to @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}. Love letters to Arethne – Enoch documents his finances drying up as he struggles to acquire the last pieces of furniture holding the sister spirits of Arethne. He laments he must soon turn to theft.

Puzzle: Tree names - Arethne (cherry vanity, west), Melne (pine table, north), Chryseis (maple armoire, east). If PCs inspect the partially made trees, they can determine what type of wood is needed for completion. Trees need wood scraps from the correct furniture piece, wire for the frame, and glue to hold it together. It takes 1 round to assemble wire mesh into the trunk shape, and 1 round to glue planks to the mesh to form a tree. Arethne is the most complete and tree-like, needing glue and a few cherry planks from the cherry vanity. Melne and Chryseis have trunks complete but need branches - wire, glue, and their remaining wood scraps. Melne requires the pine pool table. Chryseis requires the maple armoire.

The PC that lights a tree on fire feels a kiss on their cheek. If the three trees are assembled and burned, the dryad spirits of Arethne, Melne, and Chryseis appear before the PCs and bestow the Oath of the Dryads. The whole mansion can be lit ablaze, but to get the Oath players must complete all three trees.

Area 8: Kitchen.name: Area 8: Kitchen
Area 8: Kitchen.text:
In disarray, pots and pans are strewn about and the smell of burnt wood lingers in the air. A few cabinets remain, but almost all other wood containers have been destroyed. A butcher’s table covered in rust.

Intact Cabinets: Searching reveals 6 days of rations, 22gp3sp, and two jeweled silver goblets (3 gp).

Butcher’s Table: A cleaver is chipped and hacked, with a few metal buckets under the table. The buckets contain random rusted bits of metal, cut into bits. Metal bits can be used as rust monster bait. If used with a vial, can be thrown.

Door: Unlocked, but a sticky substance (glue) is leaking under the door from @UUID[.vvSeyZeQQ5iuYC4v]{Area 9}.

Secret Door: Cabinet with one cookbook (switch). Scratch marks on the floor. Outside, piles of rusting nails, hinges, and other odd bits.

Area 9: Storeroom.name: Area 9: Storeroom
Area 9: Storeroom.text:
Piles of planks, stacks of old destroyed furniture, and dozens of metal glue barrels.

Rust Monsters: Three @UUID[Actor.UpLhKe3BD9u53K9o]{rust monsters} wait in surprise, hiding between furniture and barrel stacks. Careful observation from outside the room can spot eaten barrels spilling glue, nullifying surprise.

Glue Barrels: Heavy to carry, but can be rolled.

Area 10: Reception Hall.name: Area 10: Reception Hall
Area 10: Reception Hall.text:
Three large spools of wire block the south door. A beautiful tapestry of a forest scene hangs on the west wall, featuring Enoch and his wife. Other paintings and mosaics also feature the couple. West door is locked. Ornate wood and iron door with a porthole looks into @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}.

Wire Spools: Large, blocking doors. Can be rolled to @UUID[.QDtWNbb83FxeJtkW]{Area 7}. Wire mesh is used for building the tree frames.

Paintings: Many paintings of the nude Mrs. Enoch, signed by Enoch.

Swords: Four +1 silver short swords are hung on the wall decoratively.

Area 11: Billiard Room.name: Area 11: Billiard Room
Area 11: Billiard Room.text:
Frescos depicting gladiatorial combat. Beneath the frescos are two large red velvet sofas, a bar table with furniture catalogs, and a doll. In the middle of the room is a large pool table, with pool cues crossed on top. Smells like smoke and yeast.

Door: Locked. Thieves’ tools or [[request 18 STR]] to open.

Bar Table: Walnut wood. Furniture catalog reveals the pool table was crafted out of lumber from Enoch’s mills. @UUID[Item.KqxPRZ3LyekzVDaS]{Dryad nesting dolls} sit on top of the table next to blocks of chalk. Empty tankards stink of stale ale.

Pine Pool Table: Destroyed into planks with attacks or crowbar. Table is large, best smashed up here.

Area 12: Bedroom.name: Area 12: Bedroom
Area 12: Bedroom.text:
Warm tapestries and quilts fill a small sitting room, leading to a comfy untouched bedroom. There is a large armoire, chests, and smaller lockers and boxes around. From a regal bed covered with a veil, a faint voice can be heard asking for Enoch.

Hickory Chest: Contains the Owlbear Costume.

Maple Armoire: Large, best broken up in the room to move planks. Destroyed with attacks or crowbar. Shatters if shoved down the stairs and alerts @UUID[Actor.kGRn9d1BPbqeWFcw]{Mrs. Warren}. [[request 18 STR]] to move the armoire safely down the stairs.

Ghost of Mrs. Warren: Corporeal. Appears as she was when she was dying of cancer years ago, before Enoch’s madness. She wears a loose white silk robe (20gp). She mistakes a PC for Enoch, and wishes to spend time with him. She asks him to send his company home, and to head upstairs with her for alone time. If refused, becomes incorporeal and attacks. Attacks if she sees PCs looting or hears them destroying her furniture. If the armoire is broken loudly while @UUID[Actor.kGRn9d1BPbqeWFcw]{Mrs. Warren} is upstairs, she will leave the PC she is with and seek out the disturbance.

Area 13: Art Studio.name: Area 13: Art Studio
Area 13: Art Studio.text:
Mrs. Warren brings one PC to the top of the tower, into the Northwest studio room. The top tower rooms are filled with easels, brushes, rolls of blank canvas, and dozens of jars of paint. One room is stacked with crates of fake wood fruit and dried flowers.

Paint Me Like One of Your French Girls: Mrs. Warren wants to be painted in the nude. She drops her towel and lays down on a couch, telling Enoch to paint her one last time before she dies. The moonlight from the open window turns her appearance from sickly and frail, to young and beautiful. She has little patience if the PC delays, and expects a painting in 3 rounds. Art supplies are abundant and the PC can ask the young Mrs. Warren to be creative. Three consecutive [[request 12 CHA]] checks are needed to complete the painting with favor, otherwise she is hostile.

Mrs. Warren can be seduced by charisma or song. Bards have advantage on all actions with Mrs. Warren. A single [[request 18 CHA]] check can be attempted to seduce the ghost and abandon the painting task, occupying the PC for 2 rounds. If failed - hostile. If at any point Mrs. Warren turns hostile because of actions below, she ignores the PC with her. Otherwise, she possesses the PC and returns to the group with surprise.

[4] Shrine of the Jaguar Princess.name: [4] Shrine of the Jaguar Princess
[4] Shrine of the Jaguar Princess.description:
Those who sail merchant vessels along the civilized waterways of the Hyborian kingdoms all speak of one pirate who fills them with terror: the Queen of the Black Coast. Renowned for her cunning and infamous for her cruelty, the corsair-queen’s flag spells death for all unfortunate enough to spy it on the horizon.

However, the Queen of the Black Coast tires of plundering jugs of ale, bundles of wheat, and spears bound for trembling conscripts. With her crew of criminals, outcasts, and exiles, she sets sail for the mouth of the forbidden Zarkheba river. It is on those treacherous banks that the hidden shrine of a long-lost civilization is rumored to house a relic cast by malevolent gods: the Golden Jaguar of Princess Nochtli.
