A grinning skull is painted onto this heavy cast iron amulet

Benefit: An undead creature wearing this amulet cannot be turned.
Amulet of Protection Against Turning.name: Amulet of Protection Against Turning

Axe of Tlacaetica.description:
The handle of this limestone axe is decorated with painted couatl feathers and wrapped with deer leather. Incantations are inked onto the leather.

Bonus: Functions as +2 greataxe. If natural 20 is scored on attack roll with this weapon, target is beheaded if it has a head.

Benefit: Wielder can cast the following spells each once: fireball, knock, telekinesis.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.j2gvzfnMGQwxqgGg]{Fireball}. Up to 3 near creatures in a group take [[/roll 4d6]] fire damage ([[request 15 DEX]] for half).

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.SHQa9bCk8v8wQweV]{Knock}. One locked or sealed door or container is opened.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.AZo6rYWOo0SHvpxZ]{Telekinesis}. One near creature is pushed against their will into a trap or hazard unless they roll [[request 15 STR]].
Axe of Tlacaetica.name: Axe of Tlacaetica

Circlet of the Clay Titans.description:
(5 charges) OOOOO

Benefit: Has 5 charges. Wearer can spend charges to create effects listed below. A power may be used more than once. Note there are not enough charges to use all three powers listed.

  • Shape Clay. 1 charge. Reform or open a volume of clay no largerthan 10’ cube.

  • Raise Clay Barrier. 2 charges. Cancel one melee, ranged, or breath attack made against wearer or ally she can see. Barrier crumbles immediately after blocking attack.

  • Petrify. 3 charges. Victim is turned to hard clay. They are entitled to a DC 15 CON check at end of each of their turns to return to normal.
Circlet of the Clay Titans.name: Circlet of the Clay Titans

Deer Leather Armor.description:
Tanned leather armor created from the hide of a sacrificial deer. Painted with the sigil of those who seek sacrifices for outer gods.

Bonus: Grants +2 to AC.

Benefit: Once per moon cycle, you may detect the most suitable candidate for a sacrifice within 10 miles.
Deer Leather Armor.name: Deer Leather Armor

Eye of Charming.description:
Preserved eye of an abominable outer god that came to the world with a scripture of terror.

Benefit: Character whose eyes were destroyed by revelation of Nahuatl can replace one or both eyes with a preserved eye. Replacing at least one eye restores her sight. In addition, she gains an eye tyrant eye ray she may use once per day. Specific ray granted depends on the eye used:

Eye of Charming: Near creature must roll [[request 15 WIS]] or take commands on charmer’s behalf for [[/roll 1d6]] rounds; cannot be commanded to harm itself.
Eye of Charming.name: Eye of Charming

Eye of Death.description:
Preserved eye of an abominable outer god that came to the world with a scripture of terror.

Benefit: Character whose eyes were destroyed by revelation of Nahuatl can replace one or both eyes with a preserved eye. Replacing at least one eye restores her sight. In addition, she gains an eye tyrant eye ray she may use once per day. Specific ray granted depends on the eye used:

Eye of Death: Near creature must roll [[request 15 CON]] or take [[/roll 3d8]] damage and lose 2 points of CON.
Eye of Death.name: Eye of Death

Eye of Scrying.description:
Preserved eye of an abominable outer god that came to the world with a scripture of terror.

Benefit: Character whose eyes were destroyed by revelation of Nahuatl can replace one or both eyes with a preserved eye. Replacing at least one eye restores her sight. In addition, she gains an eye tyrant eye ray she may use once per day. Specific ray granted depends on the eye used:

Eye of Scrying: Eye pops free and floats around at behest of owner; while flying can see magical auras and can travel up to far distance from owner.
Eye of Scrying.name: Eye of Scrying

Eye of Slumber.description:
Preserved eye of an abominable outer god that came to the world with a scripture of terror.

Benefit: Character whose eyes were destroyed by revelation of Nahuatl can replace one or both eyes with a preserved eye. Replacing at least one eye restores her sight. In addition, she gains an eye tyrant eye ray she may use once per day. Specific ray granted depends on the eye used:

Eye of Slumber: Near creature must roll [[request 15 WIS]] or fall asleep for [[/roll 1d6]] rounds.
Eye of Slumber.name: Eye of Slumber

Golden Jaguar of Nochtli.description:
Cast by the Star-Eater and given as a gift to his most faithful human princess, this immaculate golden jaguar idol possesses powers beyond mortal comprehension.

Benefit: The specific powers of the golden jaguar idol are left to the GM. However, they should be suitably campaign-altering. Consider giving the bearer of the golden jaguar the power to summon the wind, control the tides, rearrange the stars, and communicate with outer gods that dwell in visible planets.
Golden Jaguar of Nochtli.name: Golden Jaguar of Nochtli

Jade Sacrificial Dagger +2.description: A sacrificial +2 dagger with a jade hilt
Jade Sacrificial Dagger +2.name: Jade Sacrificial Dagger +2

Jaguar Bone Mace.description:
A gruesome spiked mace wrought from the polished bones of a sacred jaguar.

Bonus: Grants +2 to attack and damage rolls.

Benefit: Roll an attack against a jaguar (or part-jaguar creature) with advantage. This power recharges after a rest.
Jaguar Bone Mace.name: Jaguar Bone Mace

Lycanthropy Totem.description:
A wax totem shaped into the figure of a woman with a jaguar’s teeth, a bat’s wings, and a snake’s scales.

Benefit: When character crushes idol to invoke its magic, roll on a “Random Wilderness Encounter” or similar table from your favorite tabletop roleplaying game. Re-roll humanoid results. Until end of next moon cycle, character crushing idol becomes half that creature. Specific benefits granted are left to GM.
Lycanthropy Totem.name: Lycanthropy Totem

Mirror of Tlacaetica.description:
A mirror of dark glass inlaid with gold and jade. A sentimental possession of a vampire who can never again look upon her own face.

Benefit: Can absorb (negate) or redirect three eye ray attacks before shattering. Character attempting to redirect eye ray rolls [[request 12 DEX]] or [[request 12 INT]]. Success redirects ray at near target, failure causes bearer to be hit by ray and fail any checks ray might force.
Mirror of Tlacaetica.name: Mirror of Tlacaetica

Rod of Electrification.description:
A steel rod cast in the likeness of a feathered serpent wreathed in bolts of jade lightning.

Benefit: Character may plunge rod into pool or puddle of water. Creatures in contact with water take [[/roll 6d6]] damage, or half as much on [[request 15 DEX]] roll. Wielder of rod may “overload” it to increase damage dealt to [[/roll 6d12]]; however, if wielder rolls three or more 1’s on damage dice, rod deals its damage to her as well (or half on successful DEX roll). Usable once.
Rod of Electrification.name: Rod of Electrification

Sacred Piercing Kit of Nochtli.description:
A kit for performing a solemn labret piercing ritual, reserved only for Jaguar Princess Nochtli’s most devoted handmaidens.

Benefit: One character may use kit to give herself sacred labret piercing. Time it takes to give piercing triggers random encounter roll. If character pierced in this way darkens her lips with soot of a companion incinerated by lava-spewing idol of Xiuhuani, she gains the power below, usable once.

  • Mournful Kiss of Nochtli: One creature you kiss or bite must roll [[request 15 CON]] or be disintegrated. If victim succeeds on check, they may make an attack against you in retaliation.
Sacred Piercing Kit of Nochtli.name: Sacred Piercing Kit of Nochtli

Talisman of Ascension.description: An exceedingly rare gift bestowed on those who would not let death part them from their interstellar god.
Talisman of Ascension.name: Talisman of Ascension

Ring of Delusion.description:
An unassuming—but dangerous—ring given as punishment by cruel monarchs to those who fail them.

Curse: Characters finding this ring believe it to be a ring of poison immunity. Delusion is shattered first time wearer is affected by poison (or poison gas in Part I). The first time wearer is affected by poison while wearing ring, she must roll [[request 15 CON]] or die. Give her one last moment to take an action to warn future dungeoneers that come across her corpse about ring’s true nature (scratching out message in chalk, for example).
Ring of Delusion.name: Ring of Delusion

Potion of Extra-Healing.description:
A glass bottle with a fizzy, lemon-vanilla liquid inside.

Benefit. Regain 10 HP.
Potion of Extra-Healing.name: Potion of Extra-Healing

Potion of Gaseous Form.description:
You and your gear turn into a cloud of smoke for the spell's duration.

You can fly and pass through any gap that smoke could. You can sense the terrain and any movement around you out to a near distance.

You can't cast spells while in this form.

@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spell-effects.Item.u6apLIMU1w4EIW06]{Spell Effect: Gaseous Form}
Potion of Gaseous Form.name: Potion of Gaseous Form

Scroll of Silence.name: Scroll of Silence

Scroll of Spell Catching.description: Usable by any character. Use when targeted by one spell to try to “catch” spell. Roll [[request 12 DEX]] or [[request 12 INT]]. On a success, spell’s harmful effect is negated, and bearer may cast caught spell from scroll.
Scroll of Spell Catching.name: Scroll of Spell Catching

Animated Clay Statue.description:
The animated statue of a jaguar-masked warrior woman.

Construct. Immune to charm, poison, sleep, and morale checks.

Cursed Wounds. Damage dealt by statue cannot be healed until victim escapes poison gas filling the catacombs.
Animated Clay Statue.name: Animated Clay Statue

Caecilia.description:
An enormous gray worm that digests the bones of the dead.

AC 12, HP 18, ATK 1 bite +3 (1d6 + digestive slime), MV near (climb), S +2, D +2, C +0, I -3, W +1, Ch -3, AL N, LV 4

Attach. Attach to target; bite auto-hits next round. DC 12 STR on turn to tear off.

Digestive Slime. Victim takes 1d6 damage at start of each of their turns. Entitled to DC 15 CON check at end of each turn to end ongoing damage.
Caecilia.name: Caecilia

Fire Beetle Swarm.description:
Luminescent beetles that burn from within with pyre flame.

AC 13, HP 14, ATK 2 bite +3 (1d6 + burn scroll), MV near (fly), S -1, D +3, C +1, I -3, W +0, Ch -3, AL N, LV 3

Burn Scroll: Target must roll [[request 15 DEX]] or have one scroll they’re carrying be burned up (target’s choice).

Retreat: When one swarm is destroyed, other flees through cracks in walls. Returns later to attack party at inopportune moment of GM’s choice.
Fire Beetle Swarm.name: Fire Beetle Swarm

Retreat.name: Retreat

Iconyotl, The Devourer.description:
One of the Star-Eater’s servant demigods, manifesting as an elder flail snail. Devours relics of civilizations that oppose the Jaguar Princess.

AC 17, HP 32, ATK 2 flail +6 (2d8), MV near, S +3, D +0, C +3, I -2, W +0, Ch -2, AL C, LV 7

CRACKING THE SHELL

Inform characters that Iconyotl is protected by his shell and only takes half damage from non-bludgeoning attacks—however, bludgeoning attacks crack his shell and deal double damage. Warn characters that Iconyotl has swallowed two random potions, and that each bludgeoning attack has a 1-in-3 chance of shattering one potion. If a potion is shattered, Iconyotl benefits from it as if he quaffed it. Unshattered potions can be recovered.
Iconyotl, The Devourer.name: Iconyotl, The Devourer

Hailed as a god by the lost civilization of the Jaguar Princess, this aberration from beyond the stars manifests as a pair of conjoined eye tyrants weeping tears of molten gold.

One of the Star-Eater’s servant demigods, manifesting as an elder gibbering mouther in the shape of a giant jaguar.

Gibbering: Characters must roll [[request 15 WIS]] when first encountering Nahuatl or become @UUID[RollTable.ph9vehHldY8SCwde]{confused}. Confused characters roll on table below to determine action each turn.

Revelation: See below

REVELATION OF NAHUATL

One random character finds that they are immune to the babbling. Instead, they can understand the hurried words being spit from the hundreds of mouths in the language of outer gods.

Inform that character that she may attempt to draw close to the gibbering mouther and listen to the message being spoken. Doing so provokes 8 bite attacks, but if she survives, she receives the Revelation of Nahuatl (p. 51).

Sun Priest.description:
A wandering sun-worshipper exiled from the nearby land of Stygia. His skin is painted the same brilliant yellow as the noonday sun.

AC 14, HP 19, ATK 1 flail +4 (1d6) or 1 dart (near) +3 (1d4), MV near, S +0, D +1, C +0, I +0, W +3, Ch +2, AL L, LV 4

Spellcasting:

Tier 1—holy weapon, light, turn undead*.

Tier 2—augury, blind.

Turn Were-Jaguar Mummy: If were-jaguar mummy is present, uses first action to cast turn undead on that character.
Sun Priest.name: Sun Priest

Turn Were-Jaguar Mummy.description: If were-jaguar mummy is present, uses first action to cast turn undead on that character.
Turn Were-Jaguar Mummy.name: Turn Were-Jaguar Mummy

Tarantula-filled Jaguar Mummy.description:
One of Nochtli’s sacred jaguar pets, mummified with cornhusks and stuffed with venomous tarantulas.

AC 13, HP 13, ATK 1 bite +3 (1d4 + rotting curse), MV double near, S +2, D +3, C +0, I -2, W +1, Ch -2, AL N, LV 3

Undead: Immune to charm, poison, sleep, and morale checks.

Rotting Curse: [[request 15 CON]] or lose [[/roll 1d4]] CON each rest until rotting curse is lifted.

Tarantulas: If jaguar mummy is not killed with fire, a swarm of tarantulas emerge from remains. Nearest character must roll [[request 18 CON]] or contract Star-Eater venom (see below).

Star Eater Venom

A character afflicted with Star-Eater venom sweats profusely and begins a hideous transformation.

After 30 minutes of real time, the victim’s eyes fuse into a single central eye. She may cast dispel magic from the eye once. After 60 minutes, her hair falls out and eyestalks grow from her scalp. She may project an eye ray once, with an effect based on her vice: @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.n1I5OLR6M2e0jLbi]{sleep }(bottle), @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.0VCMisYBNpLkx28M]{charm person} (boudoir), @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.9gjMszk1mGwEcSo6]{hold person} (feast), or two @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.16XuBF2xjUnoepyp]{acid arrows} (pipe).

After 90 minutes, the victim’s body withers away and her headbecomes a blast spore. The blast spore floats under thecharacter’s control until she bumps into something, at which timethe spore explodes, dealing [[/roll 3d6]] damage to all near creatures.
Tarantula-filled Jaguar Mummy.name: Tarantula-filled Jaguar Mummy

Vampire Thrall Of Tlacaetica.description:
Once peasant women, these unfortunate souls now serve as the thralls of the vampire priestess Tlacaetica Who Beheads in Smoke.

AC 14, HP 25, ATK 1 bite +5 (1d10 + blood drain), MV near, S +3, D +2, C +2, I +1, W +0, Ch +4, AL C, LV 5

Greater Undead: Immune to morale checks. Only damaged by silver or magical sources.

Blood Drain: Target’s maximum HP is reduced by half damage dealt (rounded down). Maximum HP returns to normal after resting.

Call Mother’s Axe: If character wields Axe of Tlacaetica, thrall can click tongue to call axe to her hand unless wielder rolls [[request 18 STR]]. Thrall wields axe against characters until slain.

Were-jaguar Mystic Priestess.description:
Few mortals are permitted to step through the ebon disc into the Star-Eater’s orbital lair. From high above the world, they plan their cruel god’s next conquest.

AC 14, HP 9, ATK 1 claw +1 (1d8) or 1 spell +2, MV near, S +1, D -1, C +0, I -1, W +2, Ch +0, AL C, LV 2

Fearless

Immune to morale checks.

Conjure Vision

May cast any tier 2 or lower spell, provided that spell is thematic to a vision of underworld punishment described by characters in area 12.

Smite.name: Smite

Lay to Rest.description:
You instantly send an undead creature you touch to its final afterlife, destroying it utterly.

You can target an undead creature of LV 9 or less
Lay to Rest.name: Lay to Rest

Command.description:
You issue a verbal command to one creature in range who can understand you. The command must be one word, such as “kneel.” The target obeys the command for as long as you focus.

If your command is ever directly harmful to the creature, it may make a Charisma check vs. your last spellcasting check. On a success, the spell ends.

Pillar of Salt.description:
A creature you target turns into a statue made of hardened salt.

You can target a creature you can see of LV 5 or less.

If you successfully focus on this spell for 3 rounds in a row, the transformation becomes permanent.

Xiuhuani.description:
Gigantic, chiseled from onyx.

Depicts hideous creature with body of iguana and head of furry bat.

Impervious to damage.

25% chance of using lava breath attack once per round.

Lava Breath: DC 15 DEX check or take 100d6 damage.

Characters who are wearing a gold-dipped jaguar mask are immune to the damage.

Retreats back to statue location after 3 rounds, unless somehow stopped.

Yarecoehua, Warden Of The Jaguar Princes.description:
This centaur-like armored mummy stands nearly thirteen feet tall. It has the upper body of a tanned muscular man, the lower body of an elephant-sized jaguar, and a featureless iron mask.

AC 17, HP 38, ATK 1 feathered great-spear +7 (3d8) and 2 claw +5 (1d6), MV double near, S +5, D +1, C +2, I -3, W +1, Ch -3, AL N, LV 8

Greater Undead: Immune to morale checks. Only damaged by silver or magical sources.

Dreadful Sleep Breath: Uses on first turn, 25% chance to use on subsequent turns. Fills near-sized cube extending from Yarecoehua. [[request 15 CON]] or sleep for 5,000 years unless neutralize poison is cast.

Area 16. Jade Snare.name: Area 16. Jade Snare
Area 16. Jade Snare.text:
Narrow Corridor: Leads to statue of muscular man in feathered headdress. Statue: Holds slab. Piles of jade on slab. Giant Slug: Dead and withered at statue's feet.

  • Open Pit Trap: Leads down to@UUID[.wZdpqwJkWFehKHab]{ area 17}. Crumpled skeleton covered in melted gold visible directly under pit.

  • Jades: They’re fake—worthless cut glass. A snare to draw tomb robbers into the pit trap.

    • Remove Jades: Small square indentation set into slab. Exact size of base of onyx pyramid found in @UUID[.U3eNJDNQBeQp56XV]{area 7}.

    • Place @UUID[Item.9rkvbEOAIUOrG849]{Onyx Pyramid} in Indentation: Constellations shine from pyramid onto walls. Pressing stone upon which Pleiades (Taurus) constellation shines reveals hidden passageway to north.

Area 15. Ancestral Necropolis.name: Area 15. Ancestral Necropolis
Area 15. Ancestral Necropolis.text:
Emaciated Corpses: Stand propped in rows of alcoves in walls. Wrapped in cornhusks and stuffed with straw. Taxidermy Beasts: Stand covered in cobwebs at corpses’ feet. Fangs, snouts, and beaks. Moisture: Dripping, reeks of withered crops.

  • Meteor Fossil: Large chunk of misshapen glittering stone on plinth at west end of necropolis. Hollow center. Bears evidence that something was excavated from it—something spherical with tiny “stalks” on top.

  • Woven Tapestry: Dark cloth behind meteor fossil. Depicts Pleiades (Taurus) constellation. Character rolling [[request 15 INT]] remembers the Star-Eater was said to come from there.

  • @UUID[Actor.3KEHTdQTjICbLjqC]{Tarantula Filled Jaguar Mummies}: Three animate and attack when characters inspect meteor fossil. They attack with surprise unless characters specifically watch taxidermy beasts.

    • Treasure Inside: One jaguar mummy has a wax @UUID[Item.jlAk0fQNJFCSobBu]{lycanthropy totem} inside it, visible to characters. Warn that if jaguar mummy is damaged with fire, totem melts and is useless.

Area 21. Path of Ascension.name: Area 21. Path of Ascension
Area 21. Path of Ascension.text:
Long Hidden Corridor: Stretches nearly 200’ to north. Walls: Murals of armored warriors with upper bodies of muscular men and lower bodies of jaguars. Each depicted cutting out own heart with jade dagger and offering it to eye among stars. Dahlia Petals: Scattered across floor, grow more numerous as characters move north.

THE END?

Seeing Nochtli’s golden jaguar turn to mere stone, the characters might believe that the object of their quest was a ruse all along. The Queen of the Black Coast won’t be so easily dissuaded.

Area 22. Ebon Disc Of The First Offering.name: Area 22. Ebon Disc Of The First Offering
Area 22. Ebon Disc Of The First Offering.text:
Circular Disc: Door-sized, set into north wall, glassy darkness. Solid to touch and emits painful chill. Corpse: Boy prince, slumped against disc. Chest cut open to reveal empty rotten cavity.

  • Offer Heart: If characters cut out heart of Yarecoehua with @UUID[Item.ufFhz7sdPIadEFzW]{jade sacrificial dagger} from @UUID[.SzQFg5dBvxg40g9g]{area 18} and place it in cavity, disc becomes portal to Part III: Devoured Star.

    • Incorrect Heart: Putting any other heart in cavity triggers void of space trap (below), as does putting Yarecoehua’s heart in cavity without using jade sacrificial dagger to remove it.

    • Void of Space Trap: Disc opens to hard vacuum. Near creatures must roll [[request 18 str]] or be sucked into space. Ask characters sucked through where on the planet their skulls land and who discovers them.

    • Boy Prince Corpse: Also gets sucked into space, but miraculously falls back to earth in one piece in dense jungle. Jaguar-masked vampire thralls recover and replace heartless corpse in 1d6 days.

Area 17. Priests of Gold.name: Area 17. Priests of Gold
Area 17. Priests of Gold.text:
Clay Priests: Six sit cross-legged atop tezontle slabs. Faces painted with grinning skulls. Walls: Inlaid with mosaics depicting priests in profile performing grotesque death dance. Holes: Hundreds bored into walls, many drip with hardened melted gold.

  • Skeleton: Human skeleton covered in melted gold. Worth 50 gp.

  • Plug Holes: Characters likely do not have enough of a material like wax or clay to plug holes. However, clever characters might use fireball to melt down a clay priest and use that.

  • The ceiling above has an opening that leads to @UUID[.Tp9gfTkHJQJULD4x]{area 16}

Approach a Clay Priest: Magic mouth appears and commands character to “KNEEL, SPEAK YOUR GREED, AND PRAY THE STAR-EATER FINDS YOU WORTHY.” Molten gold begins to drip from holes in walls. @UUID[Macro.XAt6q1bkCO7YyEYi]{Disaply Magic Mouth}

  • Kneel and Speak Greed: Priest’s mouth grinds open. Random item of that character’s greed category appears in open mouth. Each character may only kneel once.

  • Molten Gold Jets: After kneeling character receives her random item, have her roll a [[/roll d6]]. If result is equal to or less than total number of items claimed from priests, jets of molten gold spray from walls unless they were plugged. All in chamber must roll [[request 18 DEX]] or take [[/roll 6d6]] fire damage (half on success).

  • Gold-Plated Corpses: Those slain by molten gold trap are turned into gold-plated “statue” with a gp value equal to 10× their maximum HP. Ask slain players the pose in which they are turned to gold.

PRIEST’S JUDGMENT

Warn characters before they kneel about the d6 roll to determine if the molten gold jet trap is triggered. Speaking their greed is a risk-versus-reward choice they must carefully consider.

Area 18. Priest-Skull Sepulcher.name: Area 18. Priest-Skull Sepulcher
Area 18. Priest-Skull Sepulcher.text:
Two Reliefs: Set into two walls that form the eastward-pointing corner of chamber. Each depicts eye tyrant, their eyestalks the points of two pentagrams. Cube-Shaped Shelves: Set into relief at each point of star. Many contain painted skulls. Central Shelf: Sits between both reliefs, displays sacrificial dagger.

Shelf Contents

Location

Contents

N1

Talking priest’s skull that woos the “most ravenous” character in the party

N2

Severed priest’s head that snores loudly

N3

Priest’s skull shattered as if hurled against stone

N4

Painted stone priest’s skull

N5

Heap of dust

Center

@UUID[Item.ufFhz7sdPIadEFzW]{Sacrificial +2 dagger with jade hilt}

S1

Priest’s skull that argues with N1 about which character is “most ravenous”

S2

Phantom priest’s skull that wails when touched

S3

Painted priest’s skull that talks… very… slowly

S4

Priest’s skull covered in blood that never dries

S5

Priest’s head withered down to the size of an orange

  • Take Sacrificial Dagger: Entire ziggurat rumbles. Ceiling above passages back to area 13 cave in, blocking retreat. Section of floor gives way, broken stone splashing down into pool in @UUID[.KPwoakx1UFT6rWB1]{area 4}.

    • Circling Back Around: Unless characters possess powerful magic to dig through cave-in or teleport back to miniature city, they must descend back into poison gas-filled catacombs and make their way back to colossal sarcophagus in @UUID[.EKE1jow4r7KAoPrV]{area 3}. GM gains 3 poison tokens when characters descend. Noise of cave-in alerts @UUID[Actor.kYVUcxY3y3YEsdJH]{Nahuatl, the Revelator} and @UUID[Actor.8wAsm69uKuD7mAt7]{vampire thralls of Tlacaetica}.

Area 19. Xiuhuani, Underworld Scourge.name: Area 19. Xiuhuani, Underworld Scourge
Area 19. Xiuhuani, Underworld Scourge.text:
Wide Steps: Lead up toward great idol. Stairs littered with corpses charred beyond recognition. Idol: Gigantic, chiseled from onyx. Depicts hideous creature with body of iguana and head of furry bat. Murals: Along steps, show women in jaguar masks riding iguana-bat creatures over mountain ranges. Smell: Active volcano.

  • Look at Murals: Women’s jaguar masks are colored in with glittering gold paint.

  • Ascend Steps: Creatures reaching top of steps without wearing gold-dipped jaguar mask trigger cascade of steaming underworld lava to issue forth from idol’s maw. All creatures on stairs must roll [[request 15 dex]] or take [[/roll 100d6]] fire damage.

    • Destroys Were-Jaguar: Were-jaguar mummy not entitled to DEX check and burns up immediately.

    • Punishment: Ask characters slain by trap to describe what punishment they suffer in the Underworld. Should relate to their chosen greed.

  • Gold-Dipped Jaguar Masks: There are presently no gold-dipped jaguar masks in the ziggurat. However, clever characters might make their own by dipping wooden masks from @UUID[.VyWYmUoITOyZmn4R]{area 1} into gold they’ve melted themselves.

  • Secret: Block can be removed from base of idol. Reveals hidden soot-caked crawl to @UUID[.RtQxhZ9tGy1OQOCZ]{area 20.}

ROLLING 100D6 DAMAGE

The average damage of 100d6 is 350, if you’d prefer not to roll one hundred dice.

Area 20. Jaguar Princess Apparition.name: Area 20. Jaguar Princess Apparition
Area 20. Jaguar Princess Apparition.text:
Chamber: Bare and cramped. Slick with mold, stagnant. Ghostly Young Woman: Wears huipil adorned with polished bones and strings of jade beads. Crown of flowers on phantom dark hair. Pets golden jaguar idol, whispers soothing words to it in ancient language.

  • Approach Young Woman: She is Nochtli, the Jaguar Princess. She looks up with sorrowful eyes. She begs characters to leave her be, as her jaguar is all that brings her peace in her lonely afterlife.

    • An Offer: If characters leave the shrine, never return, and vow to tell no one of its location, she agrees to let them keep any gold they’ve plundered.

    • Further Disturb Nocthli: She hisses like a cat and disperses. Golden jaguar idol is revealed to be an illusion—it’s crudely chiseled tezontle. @UUID[Actor.jYfjkpoX31rl8IXP]{Yarecoehua, Warden of the Jaguar Princess}, appears in @UUID[.tZUhbd6LsXx5aAun]{area 13} and fights to death.

Area 13. Miniature City.name: Area 13. Miniature City
Area 13. Miniature City.text:
Miniature Buildings: Temples, step pyramids, plazas, windowless hovels. All glitter in shafts of sunlight that pour through openings in ziggurat wall high above. Canals: Mostly dried, snake between waist high structures.

  • Wandering Sun-Priest: Arrives a few moments after characters, casting his rope down from one of the high openings. Attacks if one of the characters is were-jaguar mummy, otherwise roll reaction as normal. Seeks to destroy Star-Eater. Might join party for one-third share of total spoils.

  • Inspect Miniature Buildings: They’re not solid gold, but rather gold-plated tezontle. Takes five trips fully loaded to strip city of its gold plating—doing so fetches 2,500 gp. Roll on @UUID[RollTable.UoB2hqLKVMhYK3AY]{Shrine Events table} each time characters leave with gold.

  • Tiny Throne: One miniature temple among dozens has empty throne. Characters specifically looking for it find it, [[request 15 WIS]] otherwise. Putting golden jaguar princess miniature from @UUID[.E5MIu5HUxcRK5eU0]{area 2} on throne opens hidden compartment containing @UUID[Item.jgtM8AK7IJWdlzxj]{sacred piercing kit of Nochtli}.

Area 14. Temple District.name: Area 14. Temple District
Area 14. Temple District.text:
Four Miniature Temples: Sit atop islands in pond thick with brown algae. No roofs, instead open to diorama-like columned halls and engraved altars. Statuettes: Each temple has gold priestess statuette with tiny stylized jaguar mask. Altars: Open like jewelry boxes.

Note that one or more temples might have been destroyed by the Hall of Thunder trap (@UUID[.xwLXtVsqPZJDhq2q]{area 6}).

  • Open Altar: Each reveals different preserved eye of Mictlan. Consult table on next page to determine specific eye found

LEAVING THE SHRINE

Characters can use the sun-priest’s rope or their own equipment to climb out of the ziggurat through windows in the side. They can return to their ship to rest, divide treasure, and level up. The Queen of the Black Coast orders the characters back to the ziggurat after resting if they return without the golden jaguar. Each time the characters leave, roll on the Shrine Events table.

MINIATURE TEMPLES

Temple

Jaguar-masked statuette

Eye in altar

Festivals

Priestess holding wine and ribbons

@UUID[Item.wthJf19PhILN2z3X]{Slumber}

Lust

Priestess with a skirt of flowers

@UUID[Item.iLKFeXVJmlDvcGGP]{Charming}

Hunt

Priestess cutting a deer’s throat

@UUID[Item.tWGGmzVtgee0Mgf1]{Death}

Communion

Priestess kneeling in fearful prayer

@UUID[Item.kMqx55tTWk6TxwKn]{Scrying}

Part II: Her City of Gold.name: Part II: Her City of Gold
Part II: Her City of Gold.text:
DANGER LEVEL

Quiet. Check every ten crawling rounds for random encounters. If an encounter is indicated, roll on the @UUID[RollTable.UoB2hqLKVMhYK3AY]{Shrine Events table} (p. 54).

GOLD-SEALED CLAY DOORS

All doors on this level are made from hardened clay sealed with melted gold. Casting @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.SHQa9bCk8v8wQweV]{knock} or @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.j2gvzfnMGQwxqgGg]{fireball} opens a door, as does the circlet of the clay titan’s shape clay power. Chiseling away melted gold by hand to open a single door takes time, triggering a @UUID[RollTable.UoB2hqLKVMhYK3AY]{Random Encounters: City of Gold} roll.

Part I: Poisonous Catacombs.name: Part I: Poisonous Catacombs
Part I: Poisonous Catacombs.text:
SPECIAL RULE: POISON GAS

The lower chambers of the ziggurat are filled with poisonous gas the color of jade. This gas is the first thing the characters sense when they regain consciousness after tumbling down the sinkhole.

Every 30 minutes of real time, the GM gains a poison gas token. The GM also gains poison gas tokens when instructed to by the text. Poison gas tokens should be represented with green beads, dice, poker chips, or something similar.

In certain situations, the GM may spend poison gas tokens to cause some harmful effect for a character. The table on the next page describes the ways in which the GM can spend poison gas tokens.

The GM starts the adventure with three poison gas tokens.

poison gas

Cost

Effect

1

Tremors. A character drops the item they are about to use, such as a weapon, scroll, or wand. They must choose a different action to take. Fragile items like potions have a 50% chance of breaking after being dropped.

3

Dizziness and nausea. A character must roll the attack, spellcasting check, or ability check they’re about to make with disadvantage.

5

Coughing and choking. Cancel the action a character is about to make and end their turn unless they choose to push through and take 6d6 damage

Danger Level

Unsafe. Check every three crawling rounds for @UUID[RollTable.JvsZD2hCJ0LipISD]{Random encounters}.

Random Encounters

d4

Details

1

A fire beetle swarm pours out from unseen cracks

2

A clay statue animates in area 1 and stalks the characters

3

A vampire spawn of Tlacaetica escapes from one of the monoliths in area 3

4

Poison gas vents from the catacomb walls—the GM gains two poison gas tokens

Area 1. Clay Warrior Gallery.name: Area 1. Clay Warrior Gallery
Area 1. Clay Warrior Gallery.text:
Darkness: Characters regain senses atop heap of debris. All is silent except rattling of last falling pebbles and their own breathing. Rows of Clay Statues: Each depicts 8’ tall warrior-woman. Stylized wooden jaguar masks. Feathered clay spears. Loincloths.

  • @UUID[Actor.OJHxQ00QP0ZNEqeW]{Animated Clay Statues}: Three activate and attack when characters start moving through chamber. One wears and uses @UUID[Item.Rgk5HpVNJAcpwUcz]{circlet of the clay titans}. Masks can be taken.

  • Stumble through Darkness: Moving character must roll [[request 12 DEX]] or [[request 12 WIS]] or bump into animated clay statue in darkness; clay statue gets free spear attack. Check not needed if all clay statues are already in melee.

Area 2. Plaster Procession.name: Area 2. Plaster Procession
Area 2. Plaster Procession.text:
Long Passageway: Stretches seemingly endlessly into darkness. Plaster Murals: Cover tezontle walls, depict animal-headed figures hurling spears, gathering corn, erecting ziggurats. Cave-In: Blocks passage to east, corpse with skull coated in melted gold half-buried in rubble (worth 20 gp).

  • Bundles: Hundreds of small octagonal cubby holes set into murals. Each displays bundle wrapped in corn husks and tied with golden thread.

  • Stop to Search Bundles: Characters can take time to search through bundles. Each character rolls a d10 on table on next page to determine what they find. GM gains poison gas token each time party stops to search bundles. Party can search a maximum of three times.

BUNDLES

d10

Contents of Bundle

1-8

Painted teeth, worthless glass beads, wooden figurines, or papyrus books

9-10

1-in-6 [[/r d6]] chance of finding @UUID[Item.2DpeT3cAKhjFBbHq]{golden jaguar princess miniature}, otherwise one random scroll: @UUID[Item.Pu0u81d9Wi8RbCDI]{neutralize poison}, @UUID[Item.4TD8vackPVEeI6F6]{hold animal}, or @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.1kzQiWXZDs6BOVxs]{silence}

Area 3. Vampire Mist Monoliths.name: Area 3. Vampire Mist Monoliths
Area 3. Vampire Mist Monoliths.text:
Oddly Shaped Monoliths: Eight in total, polished black marble. Etched with looming image of jaguar-masked woman in body paint standing barefoot atop piles of bones. Brazier: Burns with heatless pale flame at north end of chamber. Colossal Sarcophagus: Rises in center of chamber, big enough to hold a giant.

  • Inspect Brazier: Priests recognize flame as having undead repelling properties. Functions as constant turn undead. Cannot be relit if extinguished.

  • Axe Embedded in Monolith: Northwest monolith. Headless skeleton and its severed skull lie nearby. Axe radiates magic.

  • Remove Axe: It’s the @UUID[Item.c4C6elmaDYLL7uhO]{Axe of Tlacaetica}. Writing on axe reads “Tlacaetica, Who Beheads in Smoke.”

  • Vampire Mist: Unknown to characters, monoliths are hollow and contain @UUID[Actor.8wAsm69uKuD7mAt7]{vampire thralls of Tlacaetica} in mist form. One escapes through gouge if axe is pried free. Poison gas makes vampire thrall invisible, but won’t attack unless pale flame is extinguished.

  • Giant Sarcophagus: Filled with human skeletons stained green by poison gas. Each died during 5,000 year sleep. One skeleton clutches scroll of protection from felines.

Area 4. Embalming Bath.name: Area 4. Embalming Bath
Area 4. Embalming Bath.text:
Bath: Diamond-shaped pool framed by polished ochre marble. Water has perfume scent despite being centuries old. Reagents: Clay bottles, oils, bowls sit along rim of pool. Mosaics: Dark-haired women sending cornhusk-mummified bodies over waterfall in canoes.

  • Treasure in Pool: Scattered along bottom are turquoise beads worth 100 gp, +2 deer-leather armor, and clay-stoppered tube containing scroll of spell catching.

  • Embalming Ritual: Clay barrels contain symbol-inked cornhusk wrappings and jars of paste. Party can use wrappings, paste, and reagents to turn one character into were-jaguar mummy (see next page).

  • Ritual Takes Time: GM gains 2 poison gas tokens.

WERE-JAGUAR MUMMIFICATION

  • Character is considered undead.

  • Immune to poison gas.

  • Half damage from non-magical or non-silvered sources.

  • Double damage from fire.

  • Agility grants +2 AC.

  • Gain extra bite attack each turn, deals 1d8 damage and is considered a magical attack.

Area 5. Nahuatl the Revelator.name: Area 5. Nahuatl the Revelator
Area 5. Nahuatl the Revelator.text:
Two Statues: Women in huipils, arms fallen away to rubble. Mosaic Circle: In center of floor, depicts winged serpent wreathed in lightning bolts. Sound: Low muttering of a hundred voices.

  • @UUID[Actor.kYVUcxY3y3YEsdJH]{Nahuatl, the Revelator}: Sleeping jaguar the size of an elephant. No fur, but covered in slimy pale flesh crisscrossed by veins as if turned inside out. Hundreds of straining eyes and fanged mouths twitch on body. He is an elder gibbering mouther jaguar.

  • Sneak Past: [[request 18 DEX]] or wake up Nahuatl.

Area 6. Hall of Thunder.name: Area 6. Hall of Thunder
Area 6. Hall of Thunder.text:
Stone Faces: Large and protrude from walls. Wolves, eagles, bison, axolotls, and jaguars. Once-vibrant paint peels to reveal cracked limestone underneath. Murals: On walls between faces. Depict women in stylized jaguar masks raising hands toward ziggurat struck by lightning. Smell: Rain.

  • Trap Demonstration: When characters first look into hall, cave creeper scuttles into passageway from opposite site. Wriggles toward characters, but hesitates when stone animal faces grind open. Calamitous sound of thunder reverberates from mouths, blasting apart cave creeper. Check for random encounter because of sound.

  • Pass without Jaguar Mask: Stone faces grind open, forceful sound of thunder blasts from mouths. All in hallway must roll [[request 18 CON]] or take [[/r 6d6]] damage. Potions shatter. Curtains of dust fall from ceiling. Check for random encounter.

    • Temple Collapse: Ask triggering character their vice. Announce that “THE [TEMPLE] IN THE CITY OF GOLD HAS COLLAPSED,” @UUID[Macro.IXvveMvqWBFPOWOB]{Display Temple Collapse Message} where [TEMPLE] is one of the options listed below that matches triggering character’s vice. Unknown to characters, a miniature building in Part II: Her City of Gold has been destroyed, along with treasure it contained.

TEMPLE COLLAPSE

Vice

Collapsed miniature temple

The Bottle

Temple of Festivals

The Boudoir

Temple of Lust

The Feast

Temple of the Hunt

The Pipe

Temple of Communion

Area 7. Expired Brazier.name: Area 7. Expired Brazier
Area 7. Expired Brazier.text:
Limestone Brazier: Large bands of gold inlaid along rim. Filled with cobwebs and disintegrated coals.

  • @UUID[Actor.pdLg9HFIMdBlNb9g]{Caecilia}: Waits curled up inside brazier, hidden beneath thick cobwebs. Attacks when disturbed.

  • Pry Free Gold Inlay: Worth 300 gp.

  • Cut Open Caecilia: Digestive tract contains @UUID[Item.JPny3s5V3g5uClbd]{gold anklet} worth 400 gp and @UUID[Item.9rkvbEOAIUOrG849]{onyx pyramid} struck through with nebula patterns.

Area 8. Nahuacoh, Root of the World.name: Area 8. Nahuacoh, Root of the World
Area 8. Nahuacoh, Root of the World.text:
Square Pillars: Painted with family trees. Path of Onyx Stones: Runs down center of hall toward head of chamber. Ancient Tree: Weeping gnarled branches the color of coal, rises from bare clay at south end of onyx path. Dahlia Petals: Cover the floor.

  • Approach Tree: Face appears in bark and yawns. Branches stretch, causing more dahlia petals to fall. Identifies himself as Nahuacoh, the Root of the World.

  • Roleplaying: Nahuacoh laments that bloodline of Jaguar Princess is down to a trickle. He assumes characters are her last descendants. He asks characters to lift his spirits by describing how each intends to find mates to bear sacred children.

    • Indulge Nahuacoh: Rewards characters by absorbing (dismissing) one poison gas token per character—two if that character thought to work their vice into their answer. Also emits glowing dahlia petals that fully heal characters.

    • Treasure: @UUID[Item.ean7aHnWrZeFt95y]{Amulet of protection against turning} hangs from Nahuacoh’s branches.

    • Monolith: Stands at end of dead-end passage leading east. Made of tezontle, appears as disquieting jumble of human, beast, serpent, and bird features. Painted skull in center.

      • Press Skull: Entire ziggurat rumbles. Monolith slides down flush into floor, as does wall behind it. Path opened back to @UUID[.VyWYmUoITOyZmn4R]{area 1}. Monolith in @UUID[.79CHxxrjAzqqJpqA]{area 12} also opens. Humid breeze whips through catacombs, extinguishing pale flame brazier and all torches. (Vampire thralls can now materialize.)

      • @UUID[Item.ceSQrnHYCkFMnMxA]{Talisman of Ascension}: Appears on centermost clay warrior statue in @UUID[.VyWYmUoITOyZmn4R]{area 1} when skull is pressed. Glows through gloom, characters returning to @UUID[.VyWYmUoITOyZmn4R]{area 1} spot it immediately.

Area 9. Royal Tomb.name: Area 9. Royal Tomb
Area 9. Royal Tomb.text:
Painted Clay Figures: Size of children, stand all throughout cluster of square tombs. Limestone Slabs: Set into center of walls, depict women in feathered crowns stringing teeth onto necklaces. Bare Footprints: Faintly visible in thin layer of ash covering floor.

  • Twist Heads Off Figures: Clay figures are actually urns. Most contain damp ash, one contains necklace of polished teeth worth 20 gp and @UUID[Item.h8rSEHckdd2MVMxN]{potion of extra-healing}.

  • @UUID[Actor.K2FbCP1QvRgOGDLZ]{Fire Beetle Swarms}: Two swarms emerge from cracks in walls and attack once they sense vibration of footsteps or voices.

  • Secret Door: One wall-slab in the northernmost crypt is not limestone, but rather clay. Too tough to break down, but @UUID[Item.Rgk5HpVNJAcpwUcz]{circlet of the clay titans} can be used to part clay. Leads into hidden passageway damp with mold.

Area 10. Iconyotl, the Devourer.name: Area 10. Iconyotl, the Devourer
Area 10. Iconyotl, the Devourer.text:
Limestone Throne: Sits against west wall, caked with mold. Pools: Shallow, filled with brackish water that drips from sagging ceiling. Skeletons decay in puddles.

  • Mace: Skeleton in a pool clutches a @UUID[Item.9fme206DRwBeKjlL]{+2 jaguar bone mace}.

  • Limestone Door to South: Locked. Can be unlocked with rusted key in Iconyotl’s stomach.

  • @UUID[Actor.roWkQwv5fbrggRcb]{Iconyotl, the Devourer}: Elder flail snail with rune-etched shell. Attacks when characters enter. Characters’ reflection in his shell appear to be decomposing.

Area 11. Neried Tomb.name: Area 11. Neried Tomb
Area 11. Neried Tomb.text:
Saltwater: Drips from cracks in low ceiling. Statue: Muscular man in feathered headdress, stained from dripping saltwater. Clutches small silver coffin in thick fingers festooned with stone rings. Small Silver Coffin: Etched with likeness of diminutive woman, skin decorated with seaweed patterns. Muffled sound of woman singing inside coffin. Sealed with wax.

  • Melt Wax: Can only be melted by magical fire, pale flame from brazier, or heat of fire beetle.

  • Open Unsealed Silver Coffin: Singing of nereid wight within becomes loud and piercing. Language unknown, but characters sense song is lascivious.

    • Nereid Wight Singing Trap: Unless silence is immediately cast, all characters must roll [[request 18 WIS]]. Characters with Bottle or Boudoir vice roll with disadvantage. On a failure, character begins to sing.

    • Fracturing the Monoliths: If two or more characters fail, singing is loud enough to crack monoliths in @UUID[.EKE1jow4r7KAoPrV]{area 3}. This frees [[/r 1d4]] agitated @UUID[Actor.8wAsm69uKuD7mAt7]{vampire thralls of Tlacaetica}. Announce that “THE VAMPIRE THRALLS OF TLACAETICA HAVE ESCAPED FROM THEIR MONOLITH PRISONS.” @UUID[Macro.TidfZfpEpaZwT9xe]{Display Announcement}

    • Treasure: After resolving her song, nereid wight disintegrates. Her small silver coffin is worth 150 gp. In addition, one character can inhale dust of nereid wight to automatically succeed on one spellcasting check as if they had rolled a critical success.

Area 12. Eye of Mictlan.name: Area 12. Eye of Mictlan
Area 12. Eye of Mictlan.text:
Kneeling Stones: Four, set into floor hewn from some hard translucent substance. Dark Abyss: Swirls beneath floor. Boulder: Huge, set into south corner, made of glittering stone. Surface is pockmarked like surface of moon. Two-Pupil Jade Eye: Set into center of boulder.

  • Inspect Boulder in Wall: DC 18 INT recognizes boulder as bearing strong resemblance to eye tyrant. Eye radiates malevolent scrying magic if detected for.

  • Remove Jade Eye: Gemstone is worth 850 gp. Can be duplicated with gemstone greed. Scrying persists (unknown to characters).

  • Corpse: Sorcerer slain by poison gas slumped against wall. Under tattered cloak are @UUID[Item.3CRiwjkPridVev5Y]{potion of gaseous form}, ring of delusion (@UUID[Item.rqEYtio8e9nCpTxX]{ring of poison immunity}), and @UUID[Item.pVzE18XE05fJr88O]{rod of electrification}.

    • Enter Monolith: If character in gaseous form from potion thinks to enter monolith in area 3 through gouge left by axe, they will discover @UUID[Item.lmLn0dFgL4x451kH]{Mirror of Tlacaetica} within.

    • Kneel: Character sees Underworld scenes materialize beneath translucent floor—throngs of broken bodies under crumbling mountains, wailing figures clutching at flesh flayed by wind-blown daggers, rivers of gore stalked by giant jaguars.

    • Fitting Punishment: Ask kneeling character to briefly describe one deceased rival, enemy, or other despised person they knew, and what brutally fitting punishment that person is receiving in the Underworld. If scrying jade eye is present, their answers (unknowingly) bolster Mictlan’s jaguar-maiden thralls in @UUID[.dszXWIv1GuLgTKrF]{Part III: Devoured Star}.

    • Monolith to West: Functions similar to monolith in @UUID[.tZUhbd6LsXx5aAun]{area 8} (p. 15).

RING OF DELUSION

An unassuming—but dangerous—ring given as punishment by cruel monarchs to those who fail them.

Curse: Characters finding this ring believe it to be a ring of poison immunity. Delusion is shattered first time wearer is affected by poison (or poison gas in Part I). The first time wearer is affected by poison while wearing ring, she must roll [[request 15 CON]] or die. Give her one last moment to take an action to warn future dungeoneers that come across her corpse about ring’s true nature (scratching out message in chalk, for example).

Walls, Floor, and Ceiling: Rough-hewn meteoric rock. Circular Disk: As big as a door, set into large golden slab against wall. Golden Slab: Etched with winged lightning serpents coiled around ziggurat. Women in stylized jaguar masks dance at base of ziggurat.

  • Ebon Disk: Functions as portal back to @UUID[.e5mYedN8N6T0SwVK]{area 22} if characters defeat Mictlan, the Star-Eater and claim his conjoined central eye. Solid and freezing otherwise.

  • Dais: In center of cavern. Sitting sphinx-like atop dais is long sought-after @UUID[Item.2DpeT3cAKhjFBbHq]{Golden Jaguar of Nochtli}.

Area 24. Ebon Disc - Unknown.name: Area 24. Ebon Disc - Unknown
Area 24. Ebon Disc - Unknown.text: As @UUID[.Pxzuc3MvgXLejPEN]{area 23}, but etchings on golden slab and disc’s destination they depict are left to GM. Perhaps disc, when opened, leads to another land of the Hyborian Age—or an utterly alien world altogether.

Area 25. Ebon Disc - Fractured.text: As @UUID[.TfGXahRUx6jPHdar]{area 24}, but ebon disc is fractured. Perhaps characters can mend disc, opening portal to future adventures on worlds beyond imagination.

Area 26. Temple of the Ascended.name: Area 26. Temple of the Ascended
Area 26. Temple of the Ascended.text:
Atmosphere: Gloomy, low chants, censer smoke, bleached skulls in cave walls peeking out like ore. Seven Statues: Depict hooded figures biting into miniature planets like oranges. Opening in Floor: Nearly 50’ across, opens out to space though some force holds air in cave. Stars visible. Miniature Moons: Two moons hover above opening, each size of large boulder, conjoined as if smashed together.

  • @UUID[Actor.IwUP71gaCC4XuKDN]{Were-Jaguar Mystic Priestesses}: Three dwell in chamber. Each kneels in gloom and chants toward hovering moons. They defend moons when characters arrive.

  • @UUID[Actor.xBl3oY0cAgQ64WZ7]{Mictlan, the Star-Eater}: At start of third round of combat, misshapen central eye opens on moons. Eyestalks unfurl. Moons are in fact Mictlan, an elder conjoined eye tyrant. He fights until intruders are annihilated.

    • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.spells.Item.AZo6rYWOo0SHvpxZ]{Telekinesis}: Characters pushed into opening by Mictlan’s telekinesis eye ray must roll [[request 12 STR]] or fall into void of space and be forever lost.

    • Final Judgment: Each time character fails check against one of Mictlan’s eye rays, a hooded statue glows. If all seven statues glow, barrier preventing characters from being sucked into space disappears. Adventure ends in a lonely field of stars.

CHARACTER LEVEL

Shrine of the Jaguar Princess is a deadly sword-and-sorcery dungeon delve designed for 4th-level characters.

ADVENTURE BACKGROUND

Those who sail merchant vessels along the civilized waterways of the Hyborian kingdoms all speak of one pirate who fills them with terror: the Queen of the Black Coast. Renowned for her cunning and infamous for her cruelty, the corsair-queen’s flag spells death for all unfortunate enough to spy it on the horizon.

However, the Queen of the Black Coast tires of plundering jugs of ale, bundles of wheat, and spears bound for trembling conscripts. With her crew of criminals, outcasts, and exiles, she sets sail for the mouth of the forbidden Zarkheba river. It is on those treacherous banks that the hidden shrine of a long-lost civilization is rumored to house a relic cast by malevolent gods: the Golden Jaguar of Princess Nochtli.

ADVENTURE SUMMARY

  • @UUID[.vIieuFMeTLWUxlCn]{Part I}: Poisonous Catacombs. The characters must escape from poison gas-filled catacombs beneath the jaguar princess’s ziggurat.

  • @UUID[.uKl1QQtqp9bjKkWQ]{Part II}: Her City of Gold. The characters explore a miniature city of gold in the heart of the ziggurat.

  • @UUID[.dszXWIv1GuLgTKrF]{Part III}: Devoured Star. The characters step through a sending disc and enter the celestial lair of Mictlan, the Star-Eater

Queen of the Black Coast.name: Queen of the Black Coast
Queen of the Black Coast.text:
In this adventure, the characters are loot-hungry corsairs aboard a ship captained by a legendary pirate known as the Queen of the Black Coast.

Each member of the party must choose or roll a vice from the table below—this vice is what caused the player character to be ejected from their society, forcing them to join the Queen’s pirate crew. A character’s chosen vice makes them more susceptible to certain dangers in the shrine.

In addition, each character is driven by greed for a particular category of treasure. Each character must choose a different category from the table on the next page.

When a character finds an item from the category they have chosen, they may choose to discover a second copy of that item. For example, a character with a greed for scrolls who discovers a scroll of spell catching may say that they find another.

Each character may use this ability only once per adventure.

However, indulging in greed has a cost—eventually, the pirates’ fortunes will run out.

Each time a character indulges their greed to create a duplicate of an item they just found, each member of the party takes a cumulative –2 penalty to all checks to resist monster special attacks or trap effects.

STARTING THE ADVENTURE

The delve begins with the player characters being chased through the jungle by furious warriors in jaguar masks. When they approach the shrine—an imposing ziggurat in a steamy jungle clearing—they fall through a sinkhole into @UUID[.VyWYmUoITOyZmn4R]{area 1}.

Ending the Adventure.name: Ending the Adventure
Ending the Adventure.text:
If Mictlan is defeated, his body melts away into a acrid sludge that drains away through the circular opening in the floor. His ichor drifts through space, where he will land on another planet and reconstitute his form in 5d100 years.

The Star-Eater’s conjoined central eye remains. The characters can use it to open the ebon discs and return to their mistress, the Queen of the Black Coast, with the golden jaguar of Nochtli.

With the godly power of the golden jaguar in her hands at last, the Queen of the Black Coast will rule the seas unchallenged. The spoils of looting the hidden shrine along the Zarkheba river have made each of her corsairs wealthier than most monarchs. Those who tire of the pirate life may retire in luxury among the various peoples of the Hyborian Age.

However, there will certainly be those who retain their zeal for adventure, who wish to stay aboard and raise the black flag over lands not yet plundered by their pale mistress. And who can say what occult treasures lie beyond the ebon discs…

Overview.text:
BACKGROUND

Giants are raiding the lands of men! Death and destruction have been laid heavily upon every place these monsters have visited.

This has caused great anger in high places, and there is a call for heroes to punish the miscreant giants, or else return and put their heads upon the headsman's block!

Yet this charge is not as harsh as it may seem, for all have been fully equipped for the mission. Guides are available to help, and sport a splendid map showing exactly where the hill giant chief’s great timber fortress resides.

Furthermore, the party has been instructed to keep any and all loot they chance upon as a reward for the perils they are to face.

ROOM KEYS

The key-worded descriptions at the start of each location are safe to share with the players.

The bulleted details beneath are for the GM.

FACTIONS

Nosnra’s Band. A war band of hill giants, ogres and bugbears that follow their chief Nosnra because his cunning leads to many feasts.

Emissaries. Cloud, stone and fire giants working with Nosnra to plan future raids and support his band. Stone giants expand the dungeon and fire giants forge arms. The “higher” giants grate under the orders of Nosnra and his boorish hill giant kin, but are kept in line by Kelnam, the cloud giant.

Orc Rebels. Former slaves of Nosnra who have fled into the natural caves of the dungeon and gather arms and numbers. Follow their hateful chieftain Azuk. Wish to liberate the rest of the clan and escape.

BASE CAMP

At dusk the party arrives at a small, concealed cave near the giants' stronghold.

The cave provides relative safety provided the party avoids being followed or leaving a plain trail. There are sufficient supplies for several weeks' stay.

STEADING

Nosnra’s huge, windowless timber stronghold. It resides in a nasty area of hard rainfalls and wet fogs. Much of the clan revels in the main hall, while maids and slaves feed them and stragglers sleep off their drunk.

DUNGEON

A stone warren long predating the Steading. A deranged hill giant called The Keeper leads bugbears in watching over slaves and battling rebel orcs, while giants excavate new areas and forge weapons.

ENTRANCES

Main Gate. Area 1. Very heavy doors.

Watchtower. Area 1A. 40’ climb.

Compound. Area 22. Visible from elevation. Gates to north and east. Filled with dire wolves.

Chimneys. 20’ climb onto roof and down to hearths. All are burning.

  • Giant in Area 19 gathers 2 ogres & 10 dire wolves from Areas 21 & 22. They split up into 2 groups and patrol outside perimeter.

  • Search parties bellow upon finding intruders and try to pin them down.

Ambush. The giants lay traps and ambushes against repeated raids.

Capture. Defeated intruders are kept in Area 28 to be cooked later.

Arson. If the Steading is somehow set aflame, all feasters from Area 11 escape to Areas 52 & 53. All treasure on the Steading level is destroyed.

Cloaks and bags hang from pegs. 2 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{giants} snore beside an empty keg. More snores echo from some stairs.

  • Bags. 22 bags. Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.oRk2jhezg2rFbbR3]{Giant’s Bag} table for contents.

  • Giants. Sound asleep. If woken alert @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{giant} upstairs (Area 1A).

Area 1A. Watch Tower.name: Area 1A. Watch Tower
Area 1A. Watch Tower.text:
A giant nursing an empty flagon dozes beneath a bell.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Giant}. If alerted, rings the bell. Wears a @UUID[Item.JpCip2Biv5CE7WOZ]{gemmed belt} (140 gp).

  • Bell. Alerts entire Steading.

Area 2. Sub-chief's room.name: Area 2. Sub-chief's room
Area 2. Sub-chief's room.text:
A bear pelt hangs by some shelves. A chest sits in a corner. A fur-laden bed creaks under a dozing @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{giantess}.

  • Shelves. 9’ above the floor. Contain: @UUID[Item.ctJqJqyYxvHdSIbN]{Silver comb} (30 gp), @UUID[Item.qhMbanow6dZlhE8I]{Copper Mirror} (20 gp), @UUID[Item.EozDwyFqCj0Pz5Kb]{Pearled gold hairpin} (80 gp)

  • Chest. Contains 98 cp, 32 sp and 150 gp.

  • Giantess. 1:4 chance of waking [[/roll 1d4]], or wakes if loud noise occurs.

Area 3. Dormitory.name: Area 3. Dormitory
Area 3. Dormitory.text:
Meaty smacks and laughter precede 12 rollicking young giants.

  • @UUID[Actor.iyWCFJCAnBq5zCOF]{Young Giants}. Use @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.VrYTiPjDOH1LIEBr]{ogre} stats. Loudly playing with weapons. Noise from the room is assumed to be this.

    • Garb fits humans. Works to disguise as one of “the kids”. Fails within 20’ distance.

Area 4. Barracks.name: Area 4. Barracks
Area 4. Barracks.text:
Torches dimly light ten sets of beds and chests. Clothes hang all along the walls. In two of the beds are snoring @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{giants}.

  • Chests. First holds 11 pp (worth 110 gp).

Area 5. Maid's Chamber.name: Area 5. Maid's Chamber
Area 5. Maid's Chamber.text:
Four beds flank humble furnishings. Four giantesses in crabby aprons bicker while resting their feet.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Giantess} maids. Lead by nasty old matron (34 HP), who is inclined to fight. If matron is slain others seek peace.

    • Describe Areas 8-10, and a safe path in exchange for matron's jewelry.

  • Beds. Under matron’s bed is chest with: 3x 250 gp @UUID[Item.cq78ps88baY09eC6]{bracelets}, 300 gp and 4 potions (2x @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.magic-items.Item.jucTGEjsqJ1znHdf]{Healing}, @UUID[Item.x7HeQzeiTlbraE8X]{Poison}, @UUID[Item.E8Y4EWL0yDrHqJ6Y]{Hill Giant Control})

Area 6. Hall of the Chief.name: Area 6. Hall of the Chief
Area 6. Hall of the Chief.text:
A fireplace lights a hall adorned in hides and littered with kegs. Several seats rest under two huge tables, which hold pottery, flagons and platters.

Shields and weapons hang on the walls and above them–under-lit by the firelight–are the mounted heads of dwarves and men.

  • Fireplace. Mantle holds a brass jar (worthless) and a skull containing a @UUID[Item.qKijH592wtvk28M8]{ruby} (200 gp) hidden by a youth.

  • Shields. 8 total, 1 is a @UUID[Item.5K21R8sFVwwvTa8J]{+3 shield}.

Area 7. Wife's Chamber.name: Area 7. Wife's Chamber
Area 7. Wife's Chamber.text:
A huge bed dominates a room richly dressed in furs and rugs. There is a strong animal odor.

Two chests and a coffer sit by a table and two chairs.

  • Animal odor. From the wife’s pet brown bear. Ambushes intruders (smells them coming).

  • Chests. Contain clothing.

  • Bed. Hides a pouch with gems:

    • @UUID[Item.3Pa2MrmC4Bz1wuni]{giant sapphire} (500 gp),

    • 3x @UUID[Item.uxTSjDOjhwTIk5F2]{emeralds} (100 gp),

    • 4x @UUID[Item.gg5u3h9JtOIisalt]{pearls} (50 gp),

    • 5x @UUID[Item.pdJupkvOCUKMH0Bm]{agates} (15 gp),

    • 3x @UUID[Item.XzGz2ZHaoQhx8gov]{malachite} (15gp),

    • 7x @UUID[Item.F5v2abY8LJVpu0xl]{quartz} (5 gp)

Area 8. Chief's Chamber.name: Area 8. Chief's Chamber
Area 8. Chief's Chamber.text:
There is a bed, 2 chairs and a small table with a tun that reeks of cheap wine. Clothing hangs on pegs and beside them a thick chain is set into the wall.

An old shield and some weapons sit in a corner beside a chest.

  • Chest. Contains clothing.

  • Chain. For pet brown bear.

Area 9. Arms Room.name: Area 9. Arms Room
Area 9. Arms Room.text:
Trophies of monstrous creatures line the walls, along with fine armaments and 4 huge fur capes.

Three simple spears and a club lean over a weather-beaten cloak thrown against a wall. Under the cloak is a old rag.

  • Armaments. Two dozen items of the chief’s personal gear.

  • Capes. Worthless, except for one@UUID[Item.5zOXqZPTYbcCxT8J]{ giant otter fur} (200 gp).

  • Rag. Holds 5 @UUID[Item.lIdXQnttBsGaAcg7]{Lightning Javelins}.

Area 10. Dining Room.name: Area 10. Dining Room
Area 10. Dining Room.text:
A long table and seating is littered with mugs and scraps. Hides of great beasts line the walls. A map hangs opposite a fireplace.

  • Hides. A manticore hide conceals a door to Area 10A.

  • Map. On skin. Of the region, shows past and planned raids.

Area 10A. Hidden Room.name: Area 10A. Hidden Room
Area 10A. Hidden Room.text:
A stack of logs chokes an alcove. Beside it descend shadowy stairs.

  • Logs. Conceal 7 scroll tubes. A sealed one holds orders for next raid (in giantish) signed "Eclavdra” and plans for the Steading (minus Dungeon).

  • Stairs. Lead to Area 55.

Area 11. Great Hall.name: Area 11. Great Hall
Area 11. Great Hall.text:
Scant torches barely illuminate the walls of a 80’ long passage. Beyond, a great hall hosts trestle tables packed with reveling giants and ogres.

Barrels and tuns pungent with ale stand about, and a great fire pit roars in the center, roasting half a dozen men and orcs.

At the center of a high table sit two bejeweled giants. A gruff giant sits at their right hand and in seats of honor are a four larger giants of stony complexion and ornate dress.

A small ballista hangs on the wall directly behind them.

  • Reveling giants. See Feast Occupants table for details. Singing, laughing, arguing. Mask outside sounds.

  • Trestle tables. Full of various sorts of meat, cheese, bread, and drinking horns.

  • Ballista. Chief’s crossbow. (Near range, +4 bonus vs. large-sized). Shoots spears (2d6 damage, 6 nearby).

  • Servants and orc slaves enter the Great Hall from the west.

Feast Occupants

Occupant

Details

Quarters

Chief Nosra and wife (use @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.Om5RbAEQDbXI8MwN]{Frost Giant} and @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Hill Giant})

Both wear 4 pieces of @UUID[Item.twM0kBcrIOmEDd8P]{jewelry}, each worth 1d8 x 100 gp.

Areas 8 & 7

Sub-chief (@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Hill Giant}, 49 HP)

Wears 4 pieces of @UUID[Item.twM0kBcrIOmEDd8P]{jewelry}, each worth 1d6 x 20 gp.

Area 2

Kelnam (@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.vdCzdpAsjmYTa1ps]{Cloud Giant})

Area 14

3 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.zIaJgXifG1mIY7FM]{Stone Giants}

Area 14

24 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Hill Giants}

Each giant wears 1d4 pieces of @UUID[Item.twM0kBcrIOmEDd8P]{jewelry} worth 1d6 x 20 gp each.

Areas 4, 15 & 16

8 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.VrYTiPjDOH1LIEBr]{Ogres}

Each ogre wears 1d2 pieces of @UUID[Item.twM0kBcrIOmEDd8P]{jewelry} worth 1d2+1 x 20 gp each.

Area 21

@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.RG84tprafQTDEFCa]{Brown bear}

Beneath chief’s table. Has @UUID[Item.9CxEgThPOMof9NBe]{quartz studded collar} (100 gp).

@UUID[.6MwCQtf4cKy202nJ]{Area 8}

Area 12. Arsenal Room.name: Area 12. Arsenal Room
Area 12. Arsenal Room.text:
There are 30 helmets, 26 shields. 22 spears, 9 clubs, and 3 great axes

around the place.

  • Items fit bugbears and ogres.

Area 13. Weapons Room.name: Area 13. Weapons Room
Area 13. Weapons Room.text:
Giant spears, shields, clubs, and axes are abundant here—no fewer than 12 of each.

There are 4 great swords, 2 huge iron maces, and a sheaf of 6' long spears.

  • Spears. Giants use as javelins.

  • Shields. Leaned against the walls. Behind the 7th one checked is a @UUID[Item.BJmE3QX94i7VKBF7]{+2 Warhammer}.

  • A @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.z98LNu4yOIe1B1eg]{warhammer} out of sight in a corner has a magic mouth spell placed on it to speak to a dwarf: "Here's a kiss for you, runt!" Until it has spoken it will radiate magic very strongly.

Area 14. Guests Chamber.name: Area 14. Guests Chamber
Area 14. Guests Chamber.text:
6 beds, 7 chests, and two tables, 4 stools, and 4 chairs fill the room. Giant garments hang on pegs. A torch smolders at the west end; at the other end is an unlit torch.

  • Kelnam and the 3 stone giants (see Area 11) lodge here.

  • Unlit Torch. Kelnam’s sword @UUID[Item.HfqFEFl7BSwW94fp]{Avalanche} (see Items) disguised by an illusion (dispels on touch).

  • Beds. 4 bags tucked underneath contain a full skin of wine, 4 old sandals, and 3 small boulders.

  • Chests. Hold 5 small boulders, a crock pot, and soiled linens.

Area 15. Common Room.name: Area 15. Common Room
Area 15. Common Room.text: This place has 10 cots, 10 boxes, 4 stools, 1 table, 2 benches, and various odds and ends.

Area 16. Common Room.name: Area 16. Common Room
Area 16. Common Room.text:
Same as Area 15, plus: A few cloaks hang from the wall and on a stool rests a small chest.

  • Chest. Holds dwarven & elven ears; one has an @UUID[Item.dIWZsaa0GewAeEIq]{earring} (10 gp)

Area 17. Kitchen.name: Area 17. Kitchen
Area 17. Kitchen.text:
Giant counters flank several central tables covered in cookware & food. A smelly chute sits in the north wall.

Dozens of cowering orcs in rags rush to deliver food and utensils to 5 giantesses dressed in aprons, who are busily preparing meals. 11 young ogres assist them.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Giantesses}. Hill giants. Maids. Flee from threats crying “Help!” Bark orders at orcs; prepare meals for feast in Area 11.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.Rq4WF5z0ZBFHNLub]{Orcs}. Slaves. Flee from threats. Bring maids things demanded, take meals to Area 11 and return from there with dishes.

  • @UUID[Actor.mmvXjD6kgqMpmmXI]{Young Ogres}. 12 HP. Servants. Do menial tasks like chopping. Flee from threats crying “Help!”

  • Chute. Garbage is dropped down here to Area 56.

Area 18. Side Kitchen.name: Area 18. Side Kitchen
Area 18. Side Kitchen.text:
Stools and utensils crowd 3 tables. On one sits broken loaves of bread

Sacks and boxes emanate rich aromas of fruit and cheese. Humanoid limbs and questionable sausages hang from the rafters.

Several casks stand against a wall.

  • Orcs frequently take and deliver food from here to @UUID[.ZzZXYuozt0GfwEYP]{Area 17}.

  • Bread. Food for the maids and ogres in @UUID[.ZzZXYuozt0GfwEYP]{Area 17}.

  • Casks. Contain wine, beer & ale. Occasionally taken to @UUID[.5HzK03NeEXFwECVc]{Area 11}.

Area 18A. Kitchen Store.name: Area 18A. Kitchen Store
Area 18A. Kitchen Store.text:
Boxes and casks frame a staircase descending into darkness.

  • Staircase. Leads to Area 26.

Area 19. Servants' Quarters.name: Area 19. Servants' Quarters
Area 19. Servants' Quarters.text:
A large room is cluttered with cots, tables, stools, old clothing and junk. By the door hangs a heavy whip.

6 giantess maids coo and flirt with a flexing "handsome" giant warrior.

  • “Handsome” @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Giant}. 43 HP. Dire wolf keeper (see Area 22). Does battle in order to show off for his admirers. Won’t cry for help unless brought to 22 HP.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.sFz8XfLheORSuxxM]{Maids}. Vying for giant’s attention. Flee if in danger.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.gear.Item.GgSheZNm2cOQYpZP]{Whip}. Belongs to “handsome” giant. Causes dire wolves in Area 22 to cower and retreat.

Area 20. Orc Quarters.name: Area 20. Orc Quarters
Area 20. Orc Quarters.text:
Palettes reeking of old sweat sit amongst piles of junk. 2 orcs lie in the mess, wincing.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.Rq4WF5z0ZBFHNLub]{Orcs}. Injured from giant kicks. Desperate to recover. Happily aid benevolent parties.

    • Know of the orc rebellion. Advise that orcs in Area 45 should be hailed as friends.

    • Otherwise, they know only of the great hall (@UUID[.5HzK03NeEXFwECVc]{Area 11}) and kitchen (Areas 17 & 18).

Area 21. Ogre Quarters.name: Area 21. Ogre Quarters
Area 21. Ogre Quarters.text:
Large heaps of skins smell of unwashed bodies. At the far end sits a great iron chest.

Circled around a table littered with copper pieces are 5 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.VrYTiPjDOH1LIEBr]{ogres} drinking beer and throwing knuckle bones.

  • Skins. 22 heaps. Ogres’ beds. #15 hides a leather sack with 2 potions: @UUID[Item.5frfp8by2cGTmya1]{giant strength}, delusion (giant strength, see below).

  • Chest. Locked. Key held by the lead ogre (in Area 11). Contains 95 sp, 70 gp, and 8 pp,

  • Ogres. Rambunctious. Strongest one (34 HP) wears an @UUID[Item.uxTSjDOjhwTIk5F2]{emerald} (100 gp) on a thong around his neck.

  • Table. Has 38 cp as stakes for the game.

  • Noise from here attracts no attention whatsoever.

POTION OF DELUSION

Looks just like a potion you know…

Curse. This potion presents as another type. It passes novice visual and taste inspection.

When a creature drinks this, they are convinced they are under the effect of the presented potion, despite no effect occurring.

Area 22. Open Compound.name: Area 22. Open Compound
Area 22. Open Compound.text:
A large compound separates the Steading from a smaller structure. Roaming about are 14 monstrous dire wolves.

  • @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.fsxmTnmQ6ASZaVJ9]{Dire Wolves}. Howl. Attack any non-giant or non-ogre. Cower at sight of whip from @UUID[.63MtAVhE7gjbetrb]{Area 19}.

Area 23: Guard Room.name: Area 23: Guard Room
Area 23: Guard Room.text:
2 benches with stools line the walls. A sheaf of spears sits by the door. 7 giant shields and 4 clubs stand along the south wall. On a small central table rests a huge horn.

  • Horn. For calling dire wolves in Area 22.

Area 24: Barracks Room.name: Area 24: Barracks Room
Area 24: Barracks Room.text: A dozen beds and chests run the room. Junk is scattered over tables. Several broken weapons and dented helmets are strewn about.

Area 25: Barracks Room.name: Area 25: Barracks Room
Area 25: Barracks Room.text:
Same as @UUID[.uZcAbWcZP0mg8otg]{Area 24}, plus: An alcove off to one side harbors a cot and 3 chests. On the wall hangs a sack.

  • Alcove. Belongs to the sergeant (feasting in @UUID[.5HzK03NeEXFwECVc]{Area 11}).

  • Cot. A sack underneath contains old helmets.

  • Chests. Filled with clothing and gear for troops and sergeant. At the bottom of one are 130 gp and 8 @UUID[Item.dR0ybZRM6wXdE6DR]{lapis lazuli} (10 gp each).

  • Sack. Contains giant boots.

Dungeon (26-58).name: Dungeon (26-58)
Dungeon (26-58).text:
FEATURES

Walls. Ancient, fine masonry.

Doors. Iron-bound planks.

Floors. Stone.

Ceilings. Arched and buttressed.

  • Passages: 10’ high at edges, 17’ high at center.

  • Small rooms: 20’ high

  • Large rooms: 30' high

Caves. Wet. Fungi. Stalagmites.

  • Caverns: 20’ high

  • Caves: 10’ high

ENCOUNTERS

  • Areas 26-33 & 50-54 are unsafe. +0 to encounter table result. @UUID[Macro.jLbZooR0iXTkH2X4]{Roll Dungeon Unsafe Enounter}

  • Areas 45-47 are unsafe. +2 to encounter table result. @UUID[Macro.cheiwuDkIruJEOZN]{Roll Dungeon Unsafe Enounter (+2)}

  • Areas 50-58 are unsafe. -2 to encounter table result. @UUID[Macro.3UZeEGDuMIjhLMe1]{Roll Dungeon Unsafe Encounter (-2)}

  • Area 49 is deadly. 2:6 chance of an encounter. +5 to encounter table result. @UUID[Macro.M5D3riFLuBJyqKSa]{Roll Dungeon Deadly Encounter (+5)}

Random Encounters

d4+x

Details
